declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not require ethical approval according to local/national legislation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper documents and explains a structural contradiction in the dominant global measurement apparatuses: democracy indices, corporate human-sustainability frameworks, human-development indices. All of them declare that the human being is at the center. Yet each measures its own frame of reference with rigor (democracy, the corporate organization, the development aggregate), not the actual human who lives inside that system. The human is left at the periphery of the very apparatus that claims to place it at the center. Two paradigmatic measurement apparatuses are examined in depth: 1) the international democracy indices (V-Dem, the EIU Democracy Index, Freedom House) 2) the corporate human-sustainability frameworks (Deloitte Human Sustainability Report, human-capital metrics in ESG frameworks, Gallup engagement surveys). 3) A third apparatus, the UNDP Human Development Index, exhibits the same structural pattern in the field of aggregate human development and will be the object of specific treatment in a later piece of the program. The same void reappears, with greater consequences, in the way artificial intelligence is being measured and governed: systems that declare themselves aligned with the human without an operational definition of what that human is. This extension is developed in section 5.5.

title: Post-Conflict Repair Capacity: Organizational Silence, Ordinary Interaction, and the Social Repair of Workplace Conflict
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Post-Conflict Repair Capacity: Organizational Silence, Ordinary Interaction, and the Social Repair of Workplace Conflict
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the concept of post-conflict repair capacity to explain why workplace conflict sometimes leads to relational repair and organizational learning, while in other cases it turns into silence, avoidance, information blocking, and relational disconnection. Post-conflict repair capacity refers to the ability to resume ordinary interaction after conflict, criticism, shame, hurt, or failure without fixing the other person as a permanent threat. Such ordinary interaction includes greetings, responses, workplace conversation, work coordination, information sharing, light humor, and the minimal gestures through which people are returned to a shared social relationship.

Previous research has examined workplace conflict through psychological safety, organizational silence, abusive supervision, emotion regulation, shame, organizational learning, and defensive routines. However, less attention has been paid to what happens after conflict: how damaged interactional order is repaired, or how it fails to be repaired and becomes stabilized as silence or avoidance.
This paper reframes psychological safety not only as the confidence to speak while taking interpersonal risks, but also as the expectation that relationships remain repairable after speaking. Employees may remain silent not simply because speaking is immediately punished, but because they anticipate that ordinary interaction will not return afterward. When criticism leads to avoidance, ignored communication, exclusion from information flows, or loss of everyday recognition, silence becomes a relational structure rather than a mere absence of speech.

The paper distinguishes between repairable authority and non-repairable authority. Repairable authority can accept partial criticism, contest other parts, and return the other person to ordinary interaction. Non-repairable authority treats criticism as a threat to self-image or legitimacy and manages the relationship through silence, distance, and contact inhibition. The paper also introduces post-conflict contact inhibition to describe the condition in which speaking, responding, sharing information, or even acknowledging the other person becomes experienced as psychologically or socially dangerous.

The central claim is that the problem of workplace conflict is not that conflict occurs. The problem is that, after conflict, people may no longer be able to talk. A mature workplace is not one without conflict, but one in which people can return to ordinary interaction after conflict and transform disturbance into learning rather than silence. Post-conflict repair capacity provides a theoretical bridge between organizational silence, psychological safety, ordinary interaction, and the social repair of workplace conflict.

title: To What Extent Can Green Infrastructure Investment Mitigate China's Clean-Energy Overcapacity?
affiliations: Bruegel and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: To What Extent Can Green Infrastructure Investment Mitigate China's Clean-Energy Overcapacity?
detail.abstract: China's industrial policies have made it the global leader in the manufacturing of solar panels, wind turbines and other renewable technologies, but at the cost of severe overcapacity that is now compressing margins across the entire sector. This paper evaluates greater investment in power infrastructure as a potential solution to stimulate energy demand, reduce curtailment and alleviate the renewable tech manufacturing overcapacity problem. Using scenario analysis, we show that grid expansion provides meaningful near-term demand relief, though supply-side consolidation remains necessary to restore durable market equilibrium.

title: Default Risk Management in Impact Lending: Evidence from Student-run Microfinance Funds and CDFIs
affiliations: Emory University, , Emory University, Emory University, Emory University and Emory University

detail.title: Default Risk Management in Impact Lending: Evidence from Student-run Microfinance Funds and CDFIs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve patients, clinical data, or biomedical human-subjects research. The qualitative component consisted of informational interviews with representatives of peer impact investing funds and Community Development Financial Institutions. No formal ethics approval was sought or required for this student-led organizational research project.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This research investigates how the Emory Impact Investing Group (EIIG) can restructure its due diligence and risk management processes to mitigate default exposure. Currently, EIIG faces challenges stemming from unstandardized screening processes and extended disbursement cycles, which often delay the discovery of poor-fit candidates until late in the consulting cycle.

To address this, we employed a mixed-methods approach, beginning with a foundational literature review. We then conducted qualitative interviews with peer impact funds and Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), specifically DreamSpring, UNC’s Impact Investing Club (UNC IIC), and Northwestern’s Lending for Evanston and Northwestern Development (LEND). Quantitatively, we analyzed national revenue trends by firm size using the Small Business Credit Survey. Our analysis suggests that portfolio performance is heavily shaped during the underwriting phase and reinforced through structured post-disbursement communication.

We found that relationship-driven, holistic underwriting (prioritizing revenue stability over traditional credit scores) is the primary driver of risk management. Furthermore, delinquency is heavily concentrated early in the loan cycle, particularly in the first 90 days post-disbursement. Because smaller firms face greater revenue volatility, they carry an inherently higher default risk. However, relationship-based lending significantly improves repayment when paired with clear expectations and structured communication.

Based on these insights, we recommend two primary operational shifts. First, EIIG should replace its informal application tools with financial-specific software, such as Plaid or lower-cost alternatives, to streamline data collection and reduce borrower friction. Second, EIIG must implement a mandatory, high-touch "client stewardship" communication protocol during the first 90 days post-disbursement, utilizing a custom tracking dashboard to monitor early risk signals and maintain accountability.

title: HRM Practices and Organizational Citizenship Behaviour (OCB): Evidence from Bangladeshi Commercial Banks
affiliations: Sohar University, Jahangirnagar University, Jahangirnagar University and Sohar University

detail.title: HRM Practices and Organizational Citizenship Behaviour (OCB): Evidence from Bangladeshi Commercial Banks
detail.abstract: Human Resource Management (HRM) approaches play a critical role in enhancing the culture in organizations by inspiring employees to perform their best through practicing organizational citizenship behavior (OCB). The prime purpose of this study is to investigate the influence of four human resource practices— recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisals, and compensation on employees’ OCB in the commercial banking sector of Bangladesh. The study collected 170 samples from various commercial banks in Dhaka city to conduct the study, using a structured questionnaire. The study conducted Structural Equation Modeling PLS-SEM, which revealed that all the HRM practices have a significant positive relationship with OCB and performance appraisal, and training & development are the strongest predictors of OCB. The significance of this study is that it gives insights into commercial banks’ employees OCB and HRM practices relationship from a Bangladeshi context.

title: Self-Financing Capacity in Zero-Price Platform Markets : Scale, Monetisation, and Asymmetric Market Shares
affiliations: CNR - Intitute for Complex Systems and Ca Foscari University of Venice

detail.title: Self-Financing Capacity in Zero-Price Platform Markets : Scale, Monetisation, and Asymmetric Market Shares

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Advertising-funded platforms typically charge users zero monetary price and compete through costly user-side investments: content supply, recommendation quality, creator incentives, interface design, trust and safety, and acquisition spending. This paper asks how scale-dependent monetisation changes the level of user-side attractiveness that a platform can finance from its own operations. It represents that capacity by net operating surplus per user, $g(N)=[R(N)-C(N)]/N$.

When surplus per user rises with scale, a small market-share advantage can relax the larger platform's financing constraint, support greater user-side attractiveness, and induce further user reallocation. In a two-platform logit benchmark, the equal-share configuration remains locally robust only when this scale-financing feedback is sufficiently weak. The curvature of surplus per user then determines whether asymmetric market shares emerge gradually or whether highly asymmetric configurations can coexist with a locally stable equal-share configuration. Under power-law monetisation, the classification changes at exponent four; under exponential monetisation, it depends on market size relative to the curvature scale, so the same technology can imply different local market-share regimes in small and large markets. A compatible gradual-adjustment process gives the resulting stability landscape a precise interpretation. The mechanism complements standard explanations of platform concentration based on direct network effects, switching costs, data advantages, and strategic conduct, while identifying a distinct empirical diagnostic and a set of implications for contestability policy.

title:
Human Understanding and Artificial Intelligence 
A Dynamic Force in the International Arena
affiliations: University of Birmingham

detail.title:
Human Understanding and Artificial Intelligence 
A Dynamic Force in the International Arena
detail.abstract: Agenda 2063 envisions 'an integrated, prosperous and peaceful Africa, driven by its own citizens and representing a dynamic force in the international arena' (African Union Commission, 2015). This paper argues that the ambition rests upon a neglected foundation, namely the structures through which societies develop understanding. While African development scholarship has long emphasised endogenous institutions, intellectual autonomy and knowledge production, little attention has been given to how Artificial Intelligence is transforming these foundations. Drawing on the Four Worlds framework, the paper examines human understanding as an evolving relationship between Being, Perturbation, Meaning and Instrumentation. It argues that families, communities, religion, schools and universities have historically constituted humanity's principal structures of understanding, while Large Language Models represent a new and powerful form of instrumentation that is reshaping how knowledge is accessed, produced and communicated. The analysis locates this transformation within Africa's distinctive human ecosystem, characterised by relatively young states and markets alongside ancient, though strained, societies. It argues that the African university now occupies a pivotal position, linking inherited systems of meaning with scientific inquiry and technological change. The paper concludes that Africa's aspiration to become a dynamic force in the international arena will depend not simply upon adopting Artificial Intelligence, but upon strengthening the human institutions that cultivate understanding, judgement and wisdom. Artificial Intelligence may extend human cognition, but it cannot replace the uniquely human responsibility for meaning.

title: Africa, Infrastructure, and Complexity
affiliations: University of Birmingham

detail.title: Africa, Infrastructure, and Complexity
detail.abstract: Infrastructure has traditionally been viewed as an optimisation problem. Governments seek the right projects, economists estimate the right models and planners search for the best allocation of scarce resources. This paper argues that such thinking begins too late. Before societies can optimise, they must first learn. Infrastructure is fundamentally an investment in uncertain futures, yet the systems within which it operates continually evolve through technological change, institutional adaptation and shifting human behaviour. The central challenge is therefore not simply to explain reality, but to learn from a reality that is itself changing. Drawing on Bernard Koopman's philosophy of observation, the paper distinguishes learning through observation from learning through explanation, arguing that the former provides the broader scientific foundation within which the latter should be understood. Regression remains indispensable for explaining relationships among recognised variables, but observation determines which variables deserve explanation in the first place. The paper proposes that infrastructure appraisal should therefore evolve from a one-off exercise in optimisation into a continuous process of observation, learning and adaptation. It concludes that Africa's greatest infrastructure opportunity lies not only in building physical assets, but in building institutions capable of learning continuously. In a complex world, development depends less on finding optimal solutions than on navigating an evolving reality.

title: AI-Enabled Fraud and Its Dual Nature: A Conceptual Framework for Accounting and Auditing Practice
affiliations: University of Duisburg-Essen, Mercator School of Management, University of Duisburg-Essen - Mercator School of Management and

detail.title: AI-Enabled Fraud and Its Dual Nature: A Conceptual Framework for Accounting and Auditing Practice
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of AI on fraud detection and perpetration within accounting and auditing contexts. Drawing on agency theory, routine activities theory, and technology acceptance literature, we develop a conceptual framework that positions AI as a dual-use technology that simultaneously enabling fraud schemes while enhancing detection capabilities. We synthesize evidence on AI-enabled fraud typologies including deepfake-facilitated schemes, automated social engineering, synthetic identity fraud, and algorithmic manipulation of financial reporting. The paper proposes a tri-dimensional preparedness model encompassing technical competency, organizational alignment, and collaborative governance as essential elements for effective fraud prevention. We argue that the accounting profession faces a critical inflection point where traditional audit methodologies and fraud detection frameworks require reconceptualization to address AI-mediated risks. This work contributes to emerging technologies literature by providing theoretical grounding for understanding AI's paradoxical role in fraud ecosystems and offering insights for practitioners navigating this complex landscape.

title: The Organisational Structure of a Large Railway Company in Spain: The Rail Company of Madrid-Zaragoza-Alicante (MZA): 1900-1941
affiliations: University of Valladolid - Universidad de Valladolid and Universidad de Valladolid - Department of Finance and Accounting

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation [grant number PID2024-155796NB-I00]

publicationDetails.detailsText: Ortúñez-Goicolea, P. P., & López-Iturriaga, F. J. (2026). The organizational structure of a large railway company in Spain: the rail company of Madrid-Zaragoza-Alicante (MZA): 1900–1941. Management & Organizational History, 1–34. https://doi.org/10.1080/17449359.2026.2688255

detail.abstract: Which mechanisms can the owners of a large firm use to ensure control when the firm grows, diversifies and merges with others and they lose some ownership? We discuss the sometimes conflicting relationships among the founders, shareholders, and managers of the Madrid to Zaragoza and Alicante Railway Company, a Spanish firm that was in operation between 1856 and 1941. We review the mechanisms through which communication among the stakeholders flowed in an effort to bridge possible conflicts of interests. From a historical perspective, we also show the effectiveness of the mechanisms adopted by the owners (mainly the Rothschild family) to ensure control over the company. We highlight how the executive committee played a key role in taking control of the firm.

title: Layered Intelligence Theory in the Logic of Reality: A Process-Logical Case for Deeply Human and Deeply AI Cognition
affiliations: Astrala Advisory Services Ltd

detail.title: Layered Intelligence Theory in the Logic of Reality: A Process-Logical Case for Deeply Human and Deeply AI Cognition
detail.abstract: Conventional models of intelligence treat cognition as an inventory of separable facultieslinguistic, logical, interpersonal, emotionalthat can be measured, ranked, and trained independently (Gardner, Frames of Mind, 1983; Goleman, Emotional Intelligence, 1995). Empirical work on latent structure contradicts this partition (Visser, Ashton & Vernon, Intelligence, 2006), and neurological evidence shows that the brain operates as a single integrated system in which emotional, intuitive, and cognitive processing cannot be cleanly separated (Ezuz, Reimagining New Approaches in Teacher Professional Development, 2018). This paper introduces Layered Intelligence Theory (LIT) as a process-logical account of cognition grounded in Brenner's Logic in Reality (LIR) (Brenner, Logic in Reality, 2008). Five nested layers physiological, emotional, associative, symbolic, and integrativeemerge not as independent modules but as dialectically interdependent regimes of a single learning system. LIT is then positioned inside a dual programme, here called the Deeply Human, Deeply AI framework, arguing that the conditions Ken Robinson identified for human creativity (Robinson, Out of Our Minds, 2001; Robinson, 2006) and the conditions Ezuz identified for independent creative learning (Ezuz, 2018) are the same conditions under which artificial cognitive systems must be designed if they are to avoid collapsing into narrow expertise, taming, and hegemonic automation. The paper closes with four falsifiable predictions and an empirical research agenda.

title: Liquidity Constraints and Price Discovery in Digital Asset Markets: A Case Study of the Counter-Strike 2 Economy

detail.title: Liquidity Constraints and Price Discovery in Digital Asset Markets: A Case Study of the Counter-Strike 2 Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the sole trader and subject of the case study described in this paper. No third party or organization had any financial interest in, or influence over, the research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study describes only the author's own trading activity and relies on publicly available marketplace data (Steam Community Market). No human participants, patients, or third-party personal data were involved, so formal ethics board approval was not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All trading activity described was conducted using the author's own funds.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how structural liquidity constraints distort price discovery in digital asset markets, using the Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) Fever Case economy as a laboratory. In April 2025, following the release of the Fever Case through Valve's Armory Pass system, I bought and sold 53 Fever Cases obtained through Armory Credits. A mandatory seven-day trade restriction-a structural barrier that Valve applies to all items acquired through its store, trades, and market-prevented sale near the case's early price peak, forcing execution after the peak had passed. The resulting Liquidity Gap of 42.67% between theoretical and realized revenue shows that correct market prediction is not, on its own, sufficient for realizing profit when a structural execution barrier sits between the two. Once the acquisition cost of the underlying Armory Passes is accounted for, the true net profit on the position is smaller still than the gross figures suggest. The paper draws an explicit parallel to IPO lock-up periods in traditional finance (Field & Hanka, 2001; Brau, Carter, Christophe & Key, 2004) and argues that execution constraints of this kind should be modeled as primary variables in a trading strategy rather than treated as a secondary risk.

title: Functional Zoning Analysis of Family Spaces for Preschool Children with Disabilities in China
affiliations: University of Bologna and Università di Bologna

detail.title: Functional Zoning Analysis of Family Spaces for Preschool Children with Disabilities in China
detail.abstract: Home life comprises much of CWDs’daily activity, including sleeping, eating, playing, learning, and rehabilitation. However, evidence on home spatial organization and accessibility constraints for preschool CWDs remains limited. This study examines preschool CWDs in developing inland Chinese cities. It analyzes functional zoning in family spaces and related factors to explain how caregiving needs, child functional dependence, housing conditions, and furniture or assistive-device arrangements jointly shape home spatial organization and children’s independent activity. Using a quantitatively led design, questionnaires (n = 305) and structured interviews (n = 35) were conducted with preschool CWDs, caregivers, and relevant staff through rehabilitation and early special-education settings. Quantitative analysis applied PCA, ANOVA, and logistic regression. Interview notes were used to contextualize the quantitative findings and interpret convergent and divergent cases. The results show that 1) home spaces often form a high-use core area shaped by caregivers’ visual supervision and rapid intervention needs, and functional boundaries frequently overlap and shift; 2) indoor mobility among CWDs combines goal-oriented tasks and spontaneous exploration, while routes are constrained by spatial scale, circulation continuity, and space occupied by furniture and assistive devices; 3) children’s age, housing conditions, caregiving structure, and furniture- and assistive-device arrangements jointly affect whether stable child-specific functional zones can be established and maintained. This study provides a contextually interpreted account of how home functional zoning is shaped in families of preschool CWDs and offers an operational basis for home-space optimization. Future research will develop and test spatial optimization models to improve household adaptability and children’s independent mobility.

title: The Phantom Third Bidder: Minimum-Bid Rules and Manufactured Competition in Indian Public Procurement

detail.title: The Phantom Third Bidder: Minimum-Bid Rules and Manufactured Competition in Indian Public Procurement

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The data used in this study were scraped from public government portals and released openly by Sarthak Sidhant, with whom the author has no financial or professional relationship.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses only publicly available administrative records published by the Government of India and state governments on their e-procurement portals. No human participants, patients or private personal data were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Indian procurement rules typically require a minimum number of bids, usually three, before a government tender can be awarded. Using 3.1 million contract awards from India’s national electronic procurement system between 2012 and 2026, worth about 26 trillion rupees, I show that this safeguard produces the appearance of competition rather than competition itself. The number of bids per tender piles up sharply at exactly three: depending on the counterfactual, 36 to 73 percent of all three-bid awards are in excess of what a smooth bidding process would generate, which is at least one in eight of all awards in the country. The pile-up sits precisely where each state’s rule sits. West Bengal, where the threshold binds at three, has 69 percent of awards at exactly three bids. Kerala and Tamil Nadu, where tenders may effectively proceed with two, pile up at exactly two. Madhya Pradesh, which tolerates single bids, shows no spike at all. Matched to tender notices, awards with exactly three bids cost about 10 percent more than comparable awards with four or five bids, and moving from two bids to three saves almost nothing while moving from three to four saves ten times as much. The third bidder, in short, is often not real. Over time, single-bid awards fell from 26 percent to 7 percent of the total while the share at the minimum more than doubled, suggesting that enforcement converted visible non-competition into staged competition. The world’s most common procurement safeguard, a minimum bidder count, can manufacture the appearance of the competition it was meant to guarantee.

title: Past the Goodhart Horizon: The Architecture and Price of Welfare-Touching Escape

detail.title: Past the Goodhart Horizon: The Architecture and Price of Welfare-Touching Escape
detail.abstract: The Goodhart Horizon says the decision-relevant quantity, the welfare given back once optimization passes the welfare peak, is non-identifiable from any monitoring channel whose conditional law given the system’s trajectory does not depend on welfare. That is an impossibility. This paper is the constructive answer to the obvious next question: if you cannot see the gap from inside, how do you get past it, what does it cost, and what shape must the overseeing institution take? Three results. First, the escape requirement is a theorem. By a Blackwell comparison straight from the (OC) definition, a channel whose law given the trajectory is independent of welfare carries no decision value about welfare beyond the trajectory, so escape requires a channel whose readings depend on welfare itself. The classical internal-model and good-regulator principles are the control-theoretic lineage that makes this feel familiar, not the proof; each presupposes detectability of the regulated variable, which (OC) denies. This re-derives the shape of the escape from the (OC) definition itself and locates the genuinely new contribution of the whole program in the measure layer, the missing-mass non-identifiability, which no structural lens generates. Second, the architecture and its price. The admissible escape is a welfare-touching outcome leaf wrapped in a recursive audit hierarchy; its cost is governed by a chi-squared overlap between query-time and deploymenttime behavior, which is one-sided: internal data can expose undercoverage, while sufficiency needs an explicit worst-case allowance or welfare-touching validation. I state that price as a local, secondorder currency, not a universal identity. Third, the governance shape. Because a trajectory-only self-audit cannot certify its own welfare contribution, a stable institution that preserves non-trivial gains must import exogenous outcome-contact; mandatory external audit is one realization of that requirement, not the requirement itself. The honest through-line: no construction here recovers the gap from inside. Every one is a disciplined way to spend a scarce welfare-touching budget and to prove when it is not enough.

title: Matching Algorithm Design and Short-Horizon Price Predictability in CME Futures
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Matching Algorithm Design and Short-Horizon Price Predictability in CME Futures
detail.abstract: We analyze short-horizon directional predictability across eight CME futures instruments using 6.83 billion Market-by-Order events from 2025. A pre-registered methodology produces 10,464 model fits across 46 instrument-session cells with Bonferroni-corrected significance testing. Three findings emerge. First, the pre-registered null hypothesis of no economic exploitability was upheld, but all 46 cells exhibit statistically significant directional predictability replicating across three holdout designs (Spearman ρ > 0.97). Second, predictability varies 40-fold across cells and is associated with matching algorithm design: K-Algorithm instruments show 8.3× the predictability of FIFO instruments, mediated by a bounce rate mechanism (ρ = +0.94), and overnight sessions show 4.0× the predictability of regular trading hours. Third, the exploitability boundary is set by spread-direction arithmetic: 0/46 cells profit at retail costs, 46/46 at marketmaker costs. Simple academic signals capture a median 89.5% of ML edge, confirming that the ML apparatus primarily validates known order book mechanics. A four-mechanism leakage taxonomy and comparison to canonical microstructure signals are detailed in the paper.

title: Accounting-Based Sector Betas and the Cost of Equity in Data-Constrained Emerging Markets: A Tiered Framework for Colombia

detail.title: Accounting-Based Sector Betas and the Cost of Equity in Data-Constrained Emerging Markets: A Tiered Framework for Colombia

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It is the outcome of independent research conducted by the author.

detail.abstract: Valuation practice for non-listed firms in emerging markets requires sector-level cost-of-equity estimates in environments where market betas do not exist for most firms and accounting time series are short. We propose CAB-Ke, a tiered hierarchical framework of accounting betas for the Colombian non-financial economy that integrates a Hill-Stone profitability beta on a leave-one-out market factor, a distress-augmented beta on an aggregate default probability, a Beaver-Kettler-Scholes cross-sectional benchmark, Bayesian (Vasicek) shrinkage toward a CAPM-neutral prior, Hamada relevering, an additive sovereign-spread model in U.S. dollars, and Fisher conversion to Colombian pesos with a conservative sovereign-yield floor. The estimation uses the SIREM panel over 2007-2012 under Decree 2649 and 2015-2025 under IFRS, excluding the 2013-2014 IFRS transition. Thirty-one non-financial two-digit CIIU (Clasificacion Industrial Internacional Uniforme) sectors are analyzed; CIIU 64 and 66 are excluded because SIREM's accounting debt-to-equity does not capture deposit leverage. Under the strict symmetric academic dual-factor criterion no sector qualifies. Under the framework's asymmetric professional criterion, one sector qualifies as Tier 1 Strong Professional Evidence, eleven as Tier 2, two as Tier 3, and seventeen as Tier 4 Fallback interpreted as conservative floors. The Spearman rank correlation between CAB-Ke and Damodaran's emerging-market benchmark is +0.06, indicating complementary rather than substitute information. The sovereign floor binds for 22 of 31 sectors in Colombian pesos; U.S.-dollar Ke retains fuller sectoral discrimination and is the recommended reporting column. A supplementary partial-reconstruction bootstrap check covering 26 of the 31 sectors is consistent with the finding that the strict symmetric academic criterion continues to be unmet under any replicate count and that tier stability holds for 24 of 26 sectors; two boundary sectors shift by one tier as replicate count increases, consistent with the tier-classification design. The framework's contribution is not statistical certainty for every sector but disciplined professional estimation under uncertainty.

title: Concurrent Extremes of Drought and Exchange Rate Scissors: Re-evaluating Virtual Water Flows under Non-Linear Shocks
affiliations: and Mohammed V University of Rabat

detail.title: Concurrent Extremes of Drought and Exchange Rate Scissors: Re-evaluating Virtual Water Flows under Non-Linear Shocks
detail.abstract: Virtual water trade is increasingly shaped by synchronized stressors rather than isolated shocks. Focusing on Morocco and Türkiye, characterized by divergent exchange rate regimes and agricultural structures, we construct a dynamic, 30m resolution Virtual Water Export Volume using multi-sensor satellite imagery. Using a PPML gravity model with local projections and an Instrumental Variable approach, we examine the impact of non-linear 'concurrent extremes': the interaction between exchange rate volatility and drought on virtual water outflow embedded in agricultural exports. Results identify a complexity threshold where synchronized shocks supersede isolated climate or macro-financial stressors. We find that concurrent extremes constrain agricultural exports, overriding both the price-competitiveness gains of depreciation and the efficacy of irrigation technology, forcing a return to fundamental water-endowment trade patterns. Failing to account for non-linear compound shocks leads to significant forecasting errors within the water-food-energy nexus and highlights the need for adaptation strategies decoupled from macro-financial volatility, such as decentralized renewable energy sources.

title: Optimal Regulatory Contracts and Endogenous Firm Sorting in Public Franchises

detail.title: Optimal Regulatory Contracts and Endogenous Firm Sorting in Public Franchises

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: There are no ethical issues.
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Longitudinal Capitation, a structural mechanism design that resolves chronic agency conflicts, strategic rent-seeking, and asset degradation in publicprivate procurement franchises. By extending the classic Grossman framework to incorporate multi-tasking corporate agents, we formalize how legacy flat-fee regulation treats asset erosion as an unpriced operational externality. To rectify this market failure, our mechanism shifts the regulatory target away from static baseline compliance and onto the intertemporal velocity of asset depreciation. By tying payments to a cohort's year-overyear risk trajectory relative to a case-mix insulating baseline, the mechanism forces the firm to internalize the long-term cost of operational neglect. Importantly, the regulator does not micromanage firm behavior or dictate internal resource allocation. Instead, the mechanism establishes an information-enforced decentralized market structure; by auditing quality outcomes rather than corporate actions, the policy parameter alters the competitive landscape to induce self-selection, executing an evolutionary sorting process that forces inefficient, low-quality operators into voluntary market exit. We prove that an optimally calibrated longitudinal policy parameter eliminates strategic data manipulation, aligning the firm's decentralized optimization choices identically with the Social Planner's frontier under strict budget neutrality.

title: Gold Price Volatility and IFRS Fair Value Measurement: What It Actually Means for Finance Teams on the Ground

detail.title: Gold Price Volatility and IFRS Fair Value Measurement: What It Actually Means for Finance Teams on the Ground
detail.abstract: Gold prices have done something remarkable in the past two years. They have gone from just under $2,000 per ounce at the start of 2024 to an intraday high of $5,595 in January 2026. That is not a small move. And for anyone working in finance at a company that holds gold-whether as inventory, as a financial instrument, or as part of a commodity trading book-it raises some very real questions about financial reporting. IFRS 13 requires fair value measurement at the reporting date. In theory that is simple enough. In practice, when prices are swinging by hundreds of dollars in a single session, the accounting gets complicated fast. This paper looks at what that volatility actually means for finance teams applying IFRS 13-not from a theoretical perspective, but from the perspective of someone who has to close the books at the end of the quarter. It covers the fair value hierarchy, the specific challenges that volatile gold prices create, and some practical steps that controllers and CFOs can take to stay on the right side of both the standard and their auditors. The GCC is a particular focus, given the region's deep connection to physical gold trade.

title: Gender Differences in Self-Promotion and Career Advice
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Economics, The University of Sydney and Lund University

detail.title: Gender Differences in Self-Promotion and Career Advice
detail.abstract: We study the role of self-promotion and career advice in sustaining gender differences in labor market outcomes. We conduct a pre-registered experiment in which "advisers" advise "workers" to attempt either a more or a less ambitious task. We find that women promote themselves less than men and, as a result, are 12 percentage points less likely to be advised to choose the more ambitious task. This gender gap in advice persists across both quantitative and qualitative self-assessments and is robust to variation in advisers' information sets-including when advisers observe workers' actual performance-but is eliminated and even reversed when advisers are informed of the gender gap in self-promotion.

title: Improving Energy Price Forecasts: Autometrics with Indicator Saturation
affiliations: Babson College - Economics Division

detail.title: Improving Energy Price Forecasts: Autometrics with Indicator Saturation
detail.abstract: In this study, we evaluate Autometrics, an automated model selection method with controls for outliers and location shifts, against artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests for six monthly energy price series (WTI, Brent, Dubai, U.S. and Russian gas, Australian coal) from IMF data. Autometrics generally delivers lower RMSE/MAPE and higher directional accuracy than the ANN and random forest specifications considered here, particularly in the more volatile oil and coal markets. Autometrics also has the benefit of being interpretable in a familiar regression context as opposed to more "blackbox" machine learning. The CARDt method often delivers predictive accuracy which is not statistically different from Autometrics, but there is some evidence that simple model averaging of the two with intercept-corrected Autometrics yields further gains relative to either alone.

title: SEDG: A Synthetic Experimental Data Generator for LLM-Based Behavioral Experiments
affiliations: and University of Texas at San Antonio

detail.title: SEDG: A Synthetic Experimental Data Generator for LLM-Based Behavioral Experiments
detail.abstract:
The rising cost, time burden, and ethical constraints associated with collecting human behavioral data create persistent challenges for researchers who design, pilot, and test behavioral theories. These challenges are especially important in marketing, psychology, information systems, management, and social sciences, where experiments often require large samples, multiple conditions, repeated pretests, or sensitive manipulations. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising complementary approach by generating synthetic participant responses that can help researchers evaluate stimuli, refine survey instruments, explore theoretical predictions, and compare expected response patterns before costly human-subject data collection. However, using LLMs for this purpose often requires substantial technical expertise, including model selection, API configuration, prompt engineering, persona construction, response parsing, and reproducible data management.

SEDG (Synthetic Experimental Data Generator) is a software platform that lowers these barriers by enabling researchers to generate synthetic responses for behavioral experiments using local and cloud-based LLMs. The platform is available at https://synthstudy.vercel.app/ and is designed around the workflow of experimental researchers rather than software engineers. SEDG allows users to specify study stimuli, define survey questions, select LLM providers and models, configure generation parameters, use predefined personas, provide custom personas, or generate responses without personas. It supports diverse experimental designs and produces structured outputs for analysis, replication, and comparison across models and conditions. By integrating flexible LLM access with research-oriented prompt construction and export functionality, SEDG democratizes access to LLM-based behavioral simulation across disciplines.

title: Third Horizon Economics: Reforming or Transforming in the Wake of COVID-19
affiliations: University of York - Department of Environment and Geography

detail.title: Third Horizon Economics: Reforming or Transforming in the Wake of COVID-19

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that no conflict of interest exists.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval via the University of York.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received to carry out this research.

detail.abstract: We live in an epoch of interlinked socio-environmental crises, manifested most recently in the COVID-19 pandemic. There is increasing recognition that neoliberalism is an underlying cause and requires transforming to avoid planetary catastrophe. 'New economics' comprises diverse approaches seeking to transform economics away from neoliberalism, but these have had little synthesis to date to build the necessary 'discourse coalition'. The pandemic could provide opportunities for an economic paradigm shift, but the pandemic's overall implications for the new economics field have also received little synthesis. My overall aims in this study, with a view to new economics being mainstreamed, are therefore to synthesise new economics responses to the pandemic to understand what the pandemic presents and represents for new economics, and also to what degree new economics stances towards the economic status quo can be considered truly transformative. To fulfil these aims, I use a systematised hybrid review and Three Horizons, a heuristic for deliberating transformations, to analyse new economics literature produced during the pandemic in 2020. This is the first and most comprehensive review of its kind, and the first to use Three Horizons as an analytical framework in this way. The review shows that the pandemic emphasises many problems with the neoliberal status quo, but presents barriers and setbacks as well as opportunities for new economics. There is disagreement in the discourse about whether we maintain, reform or transform the status quo (particularly economic growth and sustainable development); some approaches (e.g. the circular economy) are associated with relatively reformist stances, whilst others (e.g. degrowth) are more transformative. The pandemic is thus a double-edged sword for new economics, and stances towards the economic status quo could be an important source of disagreement within the new economics discourse. This research makes an important contribution to new economics by suggesting how the current pandemic could be leveraged to make the economics of the third horizon – the ideal future – a just and sustainable one, as well as revealing divergences in the discourse that must be addressed to strengthen its narrative. Three Horizons can help to navigate the complexity of transformations such as that proposed by new economics, whilst providing a sense of agency and encouraging transformative intent.

title: Adapting to Drought: Agricultural Reallocation, Land Use, and Emissions in Brazil
affiliations: FGV EAESP - Sao Paulo School of Business Administration

detail.title: Adapting to Drought: Agricultural Reallocation, Land Use, and Emissions in Brazil
detail.abstract: This paper examines how producers adapt to drought and whether those responses alter the land-use and emissions footprint of agriculture. I combine a municipality-level panel for Brazil on weather, crops, livestock, irrigation, land cover, pasture quality, and greenhouse gas emissions with a Roy-type model of land-use choice. Weather shocks are measured as municipality-specific precipitation deviations and estimated with rich regional-by-year controls. Drought induces coordinated agricultural reallocation: producers shift toward more drought-resilient crops and livestock, pasture quality deteriorates, and land use adjusts along extensive and intensive margins. These responses can reduce native forest cover and increase land-use emissions. Yet the effect is not mechanical. Where adaptation capital, agricultural calendars, and previously converted land allow producers to absorb drought within the existing footprint, adjustment occurs without new forest conversion. The results show that agricultural adaptation can either reinforce or limit climate damages, depending on the margin through which producers respond.

title: Caring under constraint: Food poverty and the role of community kitchens in Germany. Lived experiences of single parents and elderly women between shame and normalisation in Berlin, Stuttgart and Tübingen
affiliations: University of Hohenheim, University of Hohenheim, Humboldt University of Berlin, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Vienna

detail.title: Caring under constraint: Food poverty and the role of community kitchens in Germany. Lived experiences of single parents and elderly women between shame and normalisation in Berlin, Stuttgart and Tübingen
detail.abstract: Germany's food system is shaped by persistent intersectional inequalities, yet food poverty has long remained marginal in public and political debate. Since the Covid-19 pandemic and rising inflation, an increasing number of households face material and social food poverty the latter referring to exclusion from food-related social participation. Despite growing prevalence, food poverty in Germany remains insufficiently researched and monitored. We argue that hunger constitutes a form of structural violence requiring an intersectional, care-sensitive analytical lens. This article draws on semi-structured interviews with professionals and volunteers in social and food work, problem-centred interviews with single parents and elderly people in Berlin, Eberswalde, Stuttgart and Tübingen, and participatory observation during shared meals. The research includes the creation of a mapping platform in those cities to provide more visibility to existing community kitchens initiatives. Our findings reveal three interlocking mechanisms: temporal injustice, shame, and normalisation that reproduce food poverty as a structurally gendered condition. We theorise community kitchens as care infrastructures: spaces that partially compensate for welfare-state gaps while simultaneously absorbing and depoliticising structural deprivation. We argue that food poverty in high-income countries requires not expanded charity, but rights-based governance frameworks that treat food provisioning as a public responsibility. Community kitchens offer a glimpse of what food systems transformation could look like but only if supported by the political will to treat food as a right and collective good, not a privilege.

title: Monetary Policy, Information Spillovers and European Syndicated Lending
affiliations: University of Bath - School of Management, ALBA Graduate Business School, National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE) and University of Lethbridge

detail.title: Monetary Policy, Information Spillovers and European Syndicated Lending

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses secondary archival data and does not involve human participants, patients, or animals. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: We show that U.S. monetary policy shocks transmit to European corporate credit conditions through two distinct and opposing channels, both of which are priced within the same loan contract. Combining a continuous-time partial-adjustment framework with a GVAR-based external-instrument design and facility-level data on European syndicated loans, we align transmitted monetary shocks with loan-contract formation and absorb rich lender, borrower, and time-varying lender heterogeneity. We document three main findings. First, European lenders separately price the operational policy-rate component and the central-bank-information component of U.S. monetary shocks, with opposite effects on loan spreads: operational tightening raises spreads, while favorable information compresses them. Second, credit quantities adjust in the same opposing directions, with operational tightening contracting loan supply and favorable information supporting larger facilities. Third, these dynamics are accompanied by systematic changes in syndicate structure, consistent with risk reallocation among lenders. The results provide evidence that international monetary spillovers operate through bank credit supply and imply that the informational content of monetary announcements is itself a cross-border transmission channel that policymakers must monitor alongside policy-rate surprises.

title: THE SACRED SILENCE SERIES: Volume II: Awareness and the Architecture of Consciousness: The Field

detail.title: THE SACRED SILENCE SERIES: Volume II: Awareness and the Architecture of Consciousness: The Field
detail.abstract:
The paper identifies informational encroachment — the unexamined accumulation of unverified inputs and conditioned interpretations — as the primary threat to Field integrity, producing a bifurcation between inherent cognitive authority and an externally compliant proxy identity. To counter this, it introduces Apophatic Inquiry, a subtractive method that removes false, coercive, or deceptive content rather than accumulating belief, culminating in Right Action. Central to this method is Sacred Silence: the Stabilized Interval between stimulus and interpretation, functioning as a cognitive firewall that improves the Field’s Noise-to-Signal Ratio.

The paper further develops Epistemological Sovereignty, Conscious Inhabitation, the Malleable Vessel, and Functional Limitation as operational principles for maintaining Field stability. The resulting condition, Inner-standing, is presented as an engineering outcome requiring continuous maintenance rather than a singular realization. The paper concludes that no external legal or ethical structure can substitute for internal regulation of perception, setting the foundation for Volume III’s turn to affirmative formation through the Seven Principles of Natural Law and the 144 Axioms.

title: Agricultural Productivity and Regional Trade Integration in West Africa
affiliations: University of Nebraska-Lincoln

detail.title: Agricultural Productivity and Regional Trade Integration in West Africa
detail.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between regional trade integration and agricultural productivity growth in West Africa. Using panel data from 1995 to 2019, we first calculate TFP growth indices and its decomposition using a non-parametric bootstrap Malmquist-DEA index then we examine its association with variables that capture trade openness, accounting for other factors such as weather variables and agricultural R&D expenditure. The results indicate an average output-weighted annual TFP growth of 1.7% for the region, primarily driven by technological change (2.2%), despite a marginal decline in technical efficiency change (-0.05%). The regression results indicate that regional trade integration is significantly associated with agricultural productivity growth. We also learn that agricultural R&D investment has played a crucial role in fostering agricultural productivity growth, while rising temperatures impacts it negatively, highlighting the sector's vulnerability to climate change. This study underscores the importance of deepening intra-regional trade under the ECOWAS framework.

title: Identification, Estimation and Inference Based on Structural Error Projection
affiliations: Zhongnan University of Economics and Law, Monash University - Department of Econometrics & Business Statistics, University of Cambridge and

detail.title: Identification, Estimation and Inference Based on Structural Error Projection
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes to project and expand the conditional mean function of the structural error given the regressors in an endogenous regression under consideration. As the projection process is semiparametric, we define this procedure as a semiparametric projection (SP) method to address endogeneity in regression models by internally constructed instrumental variables. 

The SP method is applicable to many classes of regression models associated with endogeneity, such as linear, nonlinear, and non-and semi-parametric models, and provides a simple and computationally tractable alternative to conventional instrumental variable approaches available from the existing literature. 

This paper establishes identification conditions and derives the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. It then proposes a simple LASSO selection method to examine the finite-sample performance of both the proposed method and the established theory by simulated and real data examples.

title: Interstate Solar PV Price Transmission in Australia: A Dynamic Network Perspective
affiliations: , University of Auckland Business School and University of Auckland

detail.title: Interstate Solar PV Price Transmission in Australia: A Dynamic Network Perspective
detail.abstract: Despite rapid cost declines and widespread deployment, the domestic transmission of solar photovoltaic system prices across regions within a country remains largely unexplored. This study analyses the dynamic connectedness of PV system prices across Australian states using monthly data from August 2012 to October 2025. We use the Diebold-Yilmaz spillover index to characterize the baseline inter-state price spillover network. To isolate genuine inter-state transmission from common external cost drivers, we further extract state-level price residuals after controlling for global factors including polysilicon prices and exchange rates, and reconstruct the spillover network using these purified series. The results reveal substantial time variation in inter-state price connectedness. Dynamic connectedness substantially exceeds the static connectedness measure (20.35%), remaining above 40% for more than half of the sample period and exhibiting pronounced peaks during system-wide events such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The purified spillover network remains substantial, confirming that genuine inter-state price transmission exists independently of common global cost shocks. Directional spillover analysis shows substantial heterogeneity in state-level roles. Larger markets such as New South Wales and Queensland tend to alternate between transmitting and absorbing price disturbances, whereas smaller markets including Tasmania and the Australian Capital Territory display more persistent roles as transmitters or receivers.

title: IADI: A Rules-Based Thematic Index for US-India Defence Innovation Equities Methodology, Backtest, and Index Construction Notes

detail.title: IADI: A Rules-Based Thematic Index for US-India Defence Innovation Equities Methodology, Backtest, and Index Construction Notes
detail.abstract: IADI (Indo-American Defence Innovation Index) is a rules-based thematic index tracking publicly listed US and Indian defence-innovation equities, built to address a specific product gap: no existing exchange-traded fund covers the US and Indian defence sectors together. This paper documents an independent, single-author backtesting exercise, not a peer-reviewed or institutionally validated study. The index methodology combines eligibility and liquidity screens, a minimum-variance optimizer for constituent selection, market-capitalization weighting (capped at 10%, floored at 2%), and semi-annual reconstitution with quarterly rebalancing. Over the backtest window of January 2022 to April 2026, IADI produced a Sharpe ratio of 2.44 against 1.61 for a 50/50 blend of the iShares US Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA) and a manually reconstructed Nifty India Defence Index. These results reflect a single backtest window on a hand-curated universe with no transaction costs deducted, and should not be read as a forecast of future performance.

title: From Formal Committee to Visible Oversight: Audit Committee Disclosure Change in UK Firms after Sarbanes-Oxley
affiliations: University of Essex

detail.title: From Formal Committee to Visible Oversight: Audit Committee Disclosure Change in UK Firms after Sarbanes-Oxley
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the post-Sarbanes-Oxley period was associated with changes in the narrative visibility of audit committees in UK corporate reporting. Prior SOX research has focused mainly on compliance costs, internal controls, market reactions, audit consequences, and governance outcomes. Less attention has been paid to how the audit committee itself became more publicly narrated in annual reports. Drawing on qualitative documentary analysis of annual reports and Form 20-F-related materials from ten UK-listed firms over 2000-2016, the paper compares five UK firms with US reporting exposure and five UK-only listed firms. The findings show a shift from brief, formal acknowledgement of audit committees toward fuller, more structured, and more activity-based reporting. Among SOX-exposed firms, later reports make committee expertise, independence, complaint procedures, internal-control oversight and SOX-related accountability more visible. Among UK-only firms, similar tendencies later emerge through UK governance reform, audit committee professionalisation, internal-audit visibility, external-auditor oversight, risk-management review, viability reporting, and fair, balanced, and understandable review. The paper does not claim that fuller disclosure proves more effective oversight. Instead, it argues that the audit committee became more publicly reportable: a governance actor whose legitimacy, competence and activity were increasingly narrated to external readers.

title: The Impact of Inclusive Digital Finance on Food Security in Waemu Countries: Evidence From a Dynamic Spatial Durbin Model
affiliations: , Université de Lomé - Economics and University of Lomé

detail.title: The Impact of Inclusive Digital Finance on Food Security in Waemu Countries: Evidence From a Dynamic Spatial Durbin Model
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of digital financial inclusion on food security in the WAEMU countries over the period 2014-2024. Using a panel dataset of eight countries and a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM), it assesses both the direct and spatial spillover effects of digital financial inclusion. The findings reveal that active mobile money accounts, Internet access, and the use of digital financial services significantly reduce food insecurity. Conversely, rising temperatures, food inflation, and rapid urbanization exacerbate food insecurity, whereas economic growth, agricultural irrigation, and political stability contribute to improving food security. The results also highlight significant spatial spillover effects among WAEMU countries, emphasizing the need for stronger regional cooperation in digital finance, agricultural development, and governance to achieve sustainable food security.

title: Balance-Sheet Currency Mismatch and Product-Market Competition: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Azerbaijan’s Cement Oligopoly
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Balance-Sheet Currency Mismatch and Product-Market Competition: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Azerbaijan’s Cement Oligopoly
detail.abstract: This paper exploits Azerbaijan's 2015 twin devaluations of the manat-a cumulative depreciation of approximately 99 percent against the U.S. dollar within a single calendar year-as a natural experiment to study how the currency composition of corporate liabilities transmits macroeconomic shocks into productmarket outcomes. The setting is unusually clean: a two-firm cement industry in which one producer (the subsidiary of a multinational group) financed itself entirely through foreign-currency intercompany debt, while its domestic rival financed itself with local-currency debt and shareholder equity, yet both firms faced identical demand conditions, input markets, and regulatory environments. Using hand-collected data from audited IFRS financial statements over 2010-2024, I document that the foreign-currency-indebted firm suffered an equity contraction of 44.5 percent and required seven years to recover its pre-shock revenue level, while the matched-currency rival stabilized within two years and permanently captured market leadership. Regression evidence links financial leverage to market share with an economically large and statistically robust coefficient (a one-unit increase in debt-to-equity is associated with a 35-percentage-point share loss; HAC t =-9.1), and event-study evidence around two subsequent demand shocks (COVID-19 and post-conflict reconstruction) confirms persistent asymmetries in the two firms' exposure to public versus private demand. The findings connect the balance-sheet channel of currency crises (Krugman, 1999; Céspedes, Chang, & Velasco, 2004) to the capital-structure-product-market literature (Brander & Lewis, 1986; Chevalier, 1995; Campello, 2003), and show that in concentrated markets a single financing decision-the currency denomination of debt-can permanently reallocate industry leadership.

title: Why Can High-Dimensional Heterogeneity Be Reduced in Economics? The Subject Matter of Economics and a Causal Dimensionality Reduction Principle

detail.title: Why Can High-Dimensional Heterogeneity Be Reduced in Economics? The Subject Matter of Economics and a Causal Dimensionality Reduction Principle
detail.abstract: A fundamental challenge in economic analysis is that real-world agents exhibit high-dimensional heterogeneity—consumers differ simultaneously in income, preferences, information, behavioral dispositions, and social context; firms differ in technology, organization, capability, and institutional environment—while tractable theory requires tractable representations of this complexity. Existing approaches resolve this tension either by eliminating heterogeneity through representative-agent aggregation, by preserving it fully at the cost of analytical tractability in agentbased computation, or by compressing it statistically without guaranteeing economic interpretability. This paper proposes a fourth approach grounded in a neglected observation about the subject matter of economics itself: since economics studies the production and consumption activities of human agents, all structural factors affecting market outcomes must transmit their effects through two classes of agents— consumers and producers—before influencing exchange. This causal bottleneck, which is a structural consequence of what economics studies rather than a modeling choice, implies that the full dimensionality of agent heterogeneity can be systematically projected onto three participation-relevant variables—willingness to pay (WTP) for consumers, and marginal cost (MC) and productive capacity (q) for firms—for the purpose of characterizing potential participation sets and aggregate exchange quantities. Notably, many successful modeling traditions in economics—auction theory, structural industrial organization, matching theory, step supply analysis, and, as recently emphasized, the classical approach to supply and demand—already implicitly employ this reduction without articulating a common underlying logic. This paper makes that implicit logic explicit: it provides a unified methodological interpretation of an existing but untheorized modeling practice. Unlike statistical dimensionality reduction, which compresses information based on variance patterns, causal reduction compresses information based on position in the causal architecture of market exchange. The resulting framework generates a discrete market structure— demand as a sequence of discrete points ordered by WTP, supply as a series of line segments with capacity blocks—with non-trivial formal properties including generic multiplicity of market-clearing price ranges and a structural asymmetry in which excess demand is a systematic possibility while excess supply is not a stable structural phenomenon. We derive formal propositions characterizing these properties, contrast the causal reduction with statistical dimensionality reduction, with existing causal inference tools, and with causal representation learning in machine learning, and discuss implications for evolutionary economics and structural analysis.

title: Can Adaptive Learning Platforms Improve Student Outcomes? Experimental Evidence from the Dominican Republic
affiliations: World Bank and World Bank

detail.title: Can Adaptive Learning Platforms Improve Student Outcomes? Experimental Evidence from the Dominican Republic
detail.abstract: Most students in developing countries receive grade-level instruction despite lacking prerequisite skills, a mismatch that widens learning gaps as students progress. This paper reports evidence from a randomized controlled trial across 38 classrooms and 1,333 ninth-grade students in the Dominican Republic in which classrooms were randomly assigned to one of three arms: one in which computer-adaptive learning (CAL) software replaced two of seven weekly mathematics hours, another where CAL was combined with small-group tutoring, or a business-as-usual control. CAL improved test scores by 0.29-0.31 standard deviations over six months, a magnitude on the larger end of the range of the effects documented for education technology interventions in developing countries. The addition of small-group tutoring yielded no detectable improvement over CAL alone; if anything, classrooms assigned both interventions showed smaller gains than those receiving CAL alone, though this difference is not statistically significant. Evidence on mechanisms indicates that tutoring classrooms exhibited reduced engagement with the CAL platform. These results suggest that CAL software can be effectively integrated into classroom instruction to improve learning at scale but that multiple interventions in combination may not produce additive benefits and may instead generate unintended behavioral responses that offset their effectiveness.

title: High-Dimensional Network Spillovers in Industrial Policy: A Structural DID-Leontief Framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: High-Dimensional Network Spillovers in Industrial Policy: A Structural DID-Leontief Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is based entirely on simulated network data and aggregated public input-output tables, and does not involve human participants, patients, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper formalizes a difference-indifferences (DID) estimator built on the Leontief input-output framework, in which the theoretical trajectory represents the economy's productive capacity, while the observed trajectory represents realized output as measured in the field. At baseline, the gap between the two is a diagnostic of over-or under-efficiency, not an estimation artifact. We show that net program impact is a genuine double difference of this gap, that annual and cumulative readings are related by an unconditional telescoping identity, and that cumulative net impact decomposes exactly into a program scale bias, an input-matrix distortion, and a pure factor-reallocation shock. A rising cumulative estimator is interpreted as evidence of a genuine structural impact of the program.

title: Do Public BDC Fair-Value Marks Lag Traded Credit-Market Stress? Evidence from NAV Changes, Equity Prices, and Price-to-NAV Discounts, 2021–2026
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Do Public BDC Fair-Value Marks Lag Traded Credit-Market Stress? Evidence from NAV Changes, Equity Prices, and Price-to-NAV Discounts, 2021–2026
detail.abstract: The private credit market has grown from roughly $158 billion in assets under management in 2010 to approximately $2 trillion by mid-2024, yet the timeliness of its model-based, quarterly valuations remains largely untested. This thesis asks whether the fair-value marks of private credit portfolios lag information already impounded by traded markets, using public Business Development Companies (BDCs) — the regulated segment of private credit that simultaneously reports model-based net asset values (NAV) and trades continuously as equity. On a panel of 20 public BDCs over 2021Q3–2026Q1, spanning the 2022 rate-hiking cycle and the 2023 regional-banking stress, three findings emerge. First, the contemporaneous reaction of NAV marks to credit stress is 7–8 times weaker than the reaction of equity prices to the same shock, and the gap survives winsorization, a leverage control, two-way fixed effects, and Driscoll–Kraay standard errors. Second, the NAV response is distributed over time: about 60% of the cumulative response loads on lags of one to two quarters, while prices front-load their reaction — though the strict hypothesis that marks do not move contemporaneously at all is rejected. Third, the price-to-NAV discount shows no reliable unconditional power to predict future write-downs, which cautions against reading the price reaction as purely fundamental. Taken together, the evidence is consistent with partial, time-distributed incorporation of market information into model-based marks — moderate smoothing rather than either full detachment or instantaneous efficiency — while acknowledging that the reaction gap is measured relative to the market signal, not to unobservable true value. The design relies exclusively on free public data and is fully reproducible.

title: Topological Memory of the GFC Nadir: A Regime Classifier for HYG Based on Wasserstein Proximity to Crisis Persistence Diagrams

detail.title: Topological Memory of the GFC Nadir: A Regime Classifier for HYG Based on Wasserstein Proximity to Crisis Persistence Diagrams
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a topological regime classifier for the iShares iBoxx High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYG), based on the Wasserstein-2 distance between each day’s H1 Persistence Diagram and a reference diagram computed from the 60-day window ending on the Global Financial Crisis (GFC) S&P 500 nadir (2009-03-09). The classifier identifies days on which HYG’s topological state is statistically close to the GFC nadir state, where closeness is measured by a 252-day rolling Z-score of the Wasserstein distance falling at or below −1.5. Drawing on the approach of Takagi [2026], which applies persistent homology to credit market price trajectories, we extend the framework from dynamic loop-count divergence to historical topological proximity. Whereas the earlier framework characterises the rate of structural change, the present classifier characterises the geometric similarity of the current topological state to a reference state. Using daily HYG closing-price data from April 2007 to May 2026 (4,746 trading days with computed Persistence Diagrams), we report the conditional distribution of 20-day forward S&P 500 returns under the proximity classifier. Across the full sample (n = 84), the classified days exhibit a mean forward return of +2.98% with a frequency of positive outcomes of 77.4% (binomial test against 50%: p = 2.37 × 10−7 ; one-sample t-test against zero: p = 1.92 × 10−6 ; 95% bootstrap CI for the mean: [+1.88%, +4.17%]). We report six descriptive checks of this conditional regularity: (i) stability of the reference date (the conditional frequency of positive outcomes remains at or above 70% under 7 of 9 reference shifts within ±20 trading days of 2009-03-09); (ii) parameter sensitivity (10 of 10 valid Takens embedding configurations yield a conditional frequency of positive outcomes at or above 69%); (iii) temporal stability across IS/OOS splits (3 of 3 three-splits and 4 of 5 fivesplits yield an OOS frequency greater than or equal to the IS frequency); (iv) orthogonality to the loop-count divergence indicator of Takagi [2026] (Pearson r = +0.099; zero cooccurrence over 4,746 trading days); (v) ETF specificity (the same classifier applied to JNK and LQD yields markedly different conditional distributions); (vi) the macroeconomic profile of classified days (the VIX exhibits an average decline both before and after classification dates). The exercise is descriptive throughout: it characterises a conditional return distribution under a topological regime indicator, and does not constitute a forecast, an investment recommendation, or a trading rule. Limitations regarding the reference-point selection, sample size, and the absence of an established causal mechanism are discussed in Section 6. This paper extends the topological framework developed in Takagi [2026], which applies persistent homology to HYG price trajectories via the loop-count divergence statistic. The framework places the geometric structure of HYG’s price trajectory — rather than its level or return — at the centre of the regime classification.

title: How Do Risk Mitigation Mechanisms and Structural Resilience Allow Risk-Adjustment Performance for Macro Hedge Funds During Macroeconomic Regimes?

detail.title: How Do Risk Mitigation Mechanisms and Structural Resilience Allow Risk-Adjustment Performance for Macro Hedge Funds During Macroeconomic Regimes?
detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the performance dynamics of Macro and Event-Driven hedge fund strategies across three macroeconomic regimes, which are the Expansion, Transitional, and Crisis. These regimes have been structured from the monthly returns across HFRI Index Data, while also including macroeconomic variables, such as the VIX, DXY, Gold Price Returns, S&P 500 Market Monthly Return, Federal Reserve interest rate, US 5-year treasury bill yield to classify the regimes, while also using OLS regression to identify regime-specific performance drivers, Markov Chain transition matrices to diversify on intra-regime dynamics, as well as using linear programming to construct a weighted portfolio based on the performance across the two hedge fund strategies.

Contrary to conventional assumptions around hedge fund performance, Event-Driven has been identified as the most resilient strategy, with an annualised Sharpe Ratio of 1.09 compared to -0.22 for Macro strategies during Crisis. Thanks to further data, the final portfolio allocation attributed 57% of weight towards Event-Driven strategies compared to 43% for Macro strategies, yielding an annualised Sharpe ratio of 0.58 and a mean monthly excess return of 0.27% across 96 monthly observations between January 2018 and December 2025.

title: Does the slope of the yield curve actually predict Treasury returns?
affiliations: Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia and London Business School - Institute of Finance and Accounting

detail.title: Does the slope of the yield curve actually predict Treasury returns?
detail.abstract: We observe that small-sample bias can significantly affect both constant volatility (CV) model estimates and sample Campbell-Shiller (CS) regression coefficients and that, to a large extent, the reported consistency between the two is driven mechanically by the "built-in" VAR/OLS estimate of the mean reversion matrix in the CS regression. We also find that, when CV models are fitted to yields generated by a stochastic volatility model, there is substantial bias in model-implied CS regression coefficients.

title: A Cost Is a Cost Is a Cost - Or Is It? Consistently Accounting for Costs in Health Technology Assessment
affiliations: , University of Oxford and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Cost Is a Cost Is a Cost - Or Is It? Consistently Accounting for Costs in Health Technology Assessment
