detail.abstract: We generalize the time-varying parameter (TVP) framework for environments where parameters do not change only in time but in an arbitrary number of dimensions, such as across sectors or space. Each dimension is represented as a separate graph allowing for straightforward modeling and interpretation. We derive a closed-form solution to the associated least squares problem, study conditions under which it is unique, and show how the model can easily be modified to accommodate missing values and non-varying coefficients. Our empirical application to Phillips curve modeling illustrates inflation dynamics in multiple dimensions using the EU and US data.

title: Arab National Security in the Anthropocene Era: Strategic Horizons and the Quest for a Single Security Space (2025-2035)
affiliations: Zayed University

detail.title: Arab National Security in the Anthropocene Era: Strategic Horizons and the Quest for a Single Security Space (2025-2035)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA

detail.abstract: This study examines evolving dynamics of Arab national security and forecasts developments over the next decade. It identifies key determinants, including political stability, economic resilience, military capability, and social cohesion, while accounting for geopolitical shifts, technological change, climate pressures, and global power realignments. Employing a qualitative survey design, the research draws on semi-structured interviews with 112 regional security and policy experts and applies thematic analysis. Findings indicate that limited regional cooperation and weak economic performance undermine Arab national security. Looking toward 2035, the study anticipates foreign intervention, internal instability, and significant changes in alliances and technological utilization. The research underscores the necessity of enhanced regional cooperation. It proposes strategic measures, including strengthened partnerships, increased investment in emerging technologies, and expanded intelligence sharing to improve collective security resilience across Arab states.

title: Digital Fatigue era: Rethinking the Future of Productivity
affiliations: Dibrugarh University and Dibrugarh University

detail.title: Digital Fatigue era: Rethinking the Future of Productivity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No participants involved
declarations.funderStatement: No funding recieved

detail.abstract: Digital technologies have transformed economic and organisational systems, generating substantial gains in efficiency, connectivity, and innovation. However, an emerging consequence of digitalisation that remains insufficiently explored within economic discourse is digital fatigue. Existing research has primarily examined digital fatigue as a psychological, behavioural, or organisational phenomenon, while its broader implications for productivity sustainability remain under-theorised. This conceptual short communication addresses the research question: How can digital fatigue be conceptualised as a structural economic concern affecting productivity in digitally intensive economies? Adopting an interdisciplinary conceptual approach, the article synthesises insights from economics, psychology, neuroscience, organisational studies, media studies, and human-computer interaction research. The study develops a conceptual framework linking digital intensification, cognitive overload, attentional fragmentation, decision fatigue, and reduced cognitive recovery to challenges in productivity sustainability. By repositioning digital fatigue as a structural rather than purely individual concern, the article highlights its potential implications for labour quality, decision-making efficiency, innovation capacity, and longterm economic performance. The paper contributes to emerging debates on cognitive sustainability, the future of work, and digitally mediated economic systems, while proposing directions for future empirical and policy research.

title: Stack Battles: The US-China Artificial-Intelligence Rivalry Is Moving Beyond Chips Alone
affiliations: Bruegel and Tilburg Law and Economics Center (TILEC)

detail.title: Stack Battles: The US-China Artificial-Intelligence Rivalry Is Moving Beyond Chips Alone
detail.abstract: Despite Chinese progress, the United States remains for now ahead in the race for dominance over the so-called artificial intelligence hardware stack – the resources and equipment, especially semiconductors, needed to run AI models. US multinational Nvidia is the global market leader with the best-performing AI chips. It accounts for roughly half the world’s installed AI chip stock but as much as two thirds of installed computing capacity.

title: Relational Value under the Symbolic Crisis

detail.title: Relational Value under the Symbolic Crisis
detail.abstract:
Phenomenon. Under consumer capital, desire was long produced through the signifier, building lack in symbolic form and driving the movement of desire. As the reproduction of signifiers is cheapened, creation and labor are cheapened with it, and the older work of producing lack through the signifier becomes difficult. Value moves toward what signifiers cannot reproduce, which is relation.

Diagnosis. Relation lies near the constitutive lack around which desire turns, and capital captures relational value through the same structure of desire it once worked through the signifier, rerouting desire to a substitute object and drawing off value at each rerouting.

Claims. (1) Relation is the residual scarce value in an economy of cheapened signifiers, and a relational form of value and practice, here called relational divinity, answers the symbolic limit. (2) The capture of relational value follows a formal chain that strips a relational property, reifies it, and binds it to a commodity, driven by the necessary failure of the object of desire. (3) The justice of a relational circuit is decided at its origin, its field, and within its circulation, and the reality of the relation settles none of them. (4) The turn of capital to relation is real and advanced and constitutively exploitative at once, its limit a weakness of the capital form itself. (5) Whether a good cycle can be sustained turns on ownership, on whom the surplus and the field belong to, a question the paper poses and leaves with the reader.

Cases. Three specimens are read against a criterion of generative justice, each failing at a different point. The lifestyle claim is unjust at the origin, manufacturing a lack and gating relation by purchase. The platform is unjust at the field, monopolizing the ground on which relation becomes possible. The AKB48 model is the dialectical case, just at its origin yet captured within its circulation, an advance and a limit together.

Contribution. The paper offers a Lacanian reading of relational value, joining an account of its capture to a criterion for the good cycle, and makes explicit the place of ownership. It advances no proposal, and leaves to the reader the recognition of where, in a given case, the relation stands.

title:
Testability: Factor Hierarchy Theory and Scientific Methodology for Multi-Factor Complex Systems
—Complete Empirical Evidence from Global Asset Pricing and a Cross-Disciplinary Application Paradigm
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
Testability: Factor Hierarchy Theory and Scientific Methodology for Multi-Factor Complex Systems
—Complete Empirical Evidence from Global Asset Pricing and a Cross-Disciplinary Application Paradigm
detail.abstract:
What is the relationship among factors in any complex system driven by multiple quantifiable factors? This paper advances two core propositions. The law proposition: Factors naturally fall into two tiers—rule factors determine which set of rules currently applies, and execution factors carry out pricing under the given rules. The function of a rule factor is not reflected in its direct explanatory power but in the interaction effect through which it adjusts the exposure coefficients of execution factors. When a rule factor crosses a critical threshold, the factor weights of the entire system are systematically reset. The principle proposition: Any claim about the importance of factors in a multi-factor system must satisfy testability—only after exhaustively enumerating candidate factors, testing interaction effects, and confirming structural breaks can the claim be elevated from a hypothesis to reliable knowledge. A claim that "this factor is important" without specifying "under which regime" is an incomplete proposition.
Popper's principle of falsifiability stipulates the entry criterion for scientific knowledge: a proposition must be capable of being overturned by facts. Yet the classic criticism of Popper's theory within the philosophy of science has always centered on it having "only an attitudinal principle, no operational procedure": Popper required scientists to possess a spirit of falsification but did not specify, within multi-factor empirical research, "what counts as a rigorous test." This paper proposes that science requires a second threshold—testability: a procedural standard that specifies the concrete steps of testing. Exhaustive enumeration replaces prior beliefs; interaction effects and Chow tests replace the assumption of stable coefficients; multiple verification replaces single significance. Falsifiability guards the entrance to science; testability guards the exit of scientific discovery. Together they constitute the complete chain of scientific methodology.
The universality of this methodology rests not on the physical material of the systems—financial assets or microscopic particles—but solely on their epistemological property: whether the values of factors are independent of the subjective judgment of the observer. Any data satisfying this condition—generated by natural forces or automated equipment, uncontaminated by human scoring—should be subjected to the test of factor hierarchy theory and must satisfy the requirement of testability. This paper takes the Four-Test Procedure as the current optimal operationalization of the testability principle, completes a full verification across five major financial markets, and provides an exhaustive classification of all possible configurations of factor hierarchies. A companion paper (Tang, 2026h) has independently replicated the identical factor hierarchy structure in astronomy, identifying for the first time the new structural form of "proxy rule factor." The critical phenomena of phase transitions in physics, switchable catalysis in chemistry, and master regulators in biology—these core natural-science phenomena are likewise concrete manifestations of the rule–execution hierarchy structure, and the specialized tools already existing in each discipline are functionally equivalent to the Four-Test Procedure. The ultimate contribution of this paper lies in establishing a second threshold for science after Popper's falsifiability—testability—and offering a systematic methodological response to the reproducibility crisis in science.

title: Expanding the Operating Frontier: AI Advertising Tools and Demand-Generation Operations in Platform Marketplaces
affiliations: Korea University Business School, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University and Korea University Business School

detail.title: Expanding the Operating Frontier: AI Advertising Tools and Demand-Generation Operations in Platform Marketplaces
detail.abstract: Platform marketplaces are rapidly embedding generative and agentic AI into the tools sellers use to generate demand, yet what these tools change operationally remains underexplored. Do they simply sharpen targeting within campaigns sellers already run, or do they lower the operating burden enough to make previously infeasible demand-generation activities feasible? We study the introduction of an integrated AI advertising tool that combines creative generation, audience targeting, and bid automation on a major Korean e-commerce platform, using a seller-week panel and a coarsened-exact-matched difference-indifferences design. To rule out mechanical overlap with the tool, we measure the seller's feasible operating frontier only through non-focal advertising modes, the paid channels in which the AI tool does not run. Adoption increases participation in any non-focal mode by 11.7 percentage points and in multiple modes by 3.8 points. The expansion concentrates where the operating-burden mechanism predicts, reaching 17.6 percentage points for lower-capacity-tier sellers versus 5.3 points for higher-capacity-tier sellers. An exploratory channel decomposition links this operating-frontier expansion to gains in seller gross merchandise value and in the incidence of active consumer demand. The results reframe platform AI advertising as an operating-feasibility intervention at the operations-marketing interface, one that most expands what capacity-constrained sellers can feasibly operate.

title: AI Red Teaming in Practice: From Awareness to Action
affiliations: KPMG, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management, KPMG, KPMG, KPMG, KPMG, KPMG and KPMG

detail.title: AI Red Teaming in Practice: From Awareness to Action

declarations.funderStatement: The authors wish to acknowledge support for early stages of this research from the Cybersecurity at MIT Sloan (CAMS) consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Sincere thanks to KPMG member firm professionals that contributed to this paper.

detail.abstract: AI introduces novel and amplified cybersecurity risks. Given the probabilistic nature of the systems, combined with the development process of an AI system, traditional security risks are combined with new vulnerabilities expanding the threat landscape. These new risks are not well-evaluated by traditional security testing tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). Instead, developers and security professionals must leverage red teaming concepts, building AI red teaming capabilities and processes. Traditional red teaming has long served as a critical safeguard in cybersecurity, enabling organizations to identify and remediate weaknesses before adversaries exploit them. AI red teaming is the systematic practice of testing AI systems against these risks. Unlike traditional red team exercises, which are typically bound by technical exploits, AI red teaming expands the aperture to include behavioral vulnerabilities. While many organizations have well-established processes and budgets for traditional red teaming, AI red teaming remains an emerging capability. This paper reports on a study conducted to better understand how organizations use AI red teaming. We found that many of the organizations did not conduct AI red teaming, primarily because they were in the early stages of adopting AI which created different priorities. For those that were performing AI red teaming, the data showed that it was still in the early stages of adoption. Most organizations were selectively using these practices. The findings suggest a number of actionable insights for business, AI, Cyber and IT leaders and for those building or investing in AI systems.

title: ESG Disclosure, Corporate Governance, and Firm Value: A Panel Data Analysis of Bangladeshi Listed Firms
affiliations: University of Chittagong

detail.title: ESG Disclosure, Corporate Governance, and Firm Value: A Panel Data Analysis of Bangladeshi Listed Firms
detail.abstract: This study examines the joint effect of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure and corporate governance mechanisms on firm value among 120 non-financial firms listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) over 2014–2023, yielding 1,200 firm-year observations. Using a hand-collected ESG disclosure index derived from the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) framework and annual report content analysis, we estimate fixed-effects, random-effects, and two-step system generalised method of moments (GMM) panel models to address endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, and reverse causality. Firm value is proxied by Tobin's Q. Results reveal a significant positive association between ESG disclosure and firm value, with the governance pillar exerting the strongest influence. Board independence and audit quality reinforce this relationship, whereas CEO duality attenuates it. Interaction analysis further shows that strong internal governance amplifies the market's valuation of ESG disclosure. Findings extend stakeholder, agency, and legitimacy theories to an underexplored South Asian emerging-market setting and provide evidence-based implications for regulators, boards, and institutional investors advancing sustainable capital markets in Bangladesh.

title: New Ledgers, Old Topology: A Structural Framework for Tokenized Deposit Interoperability

detail.title: New Ledgers, Old Topology: A Structural Framework for Tokenized Deposit Interoperability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a core builder of both the CBMT project (Model II) and the UDPN Kissen project (Model III). The following mitigations are applied: (1) evaluation criteria were fixed before any architecture was assessed; (2) wherever possible, claims about competing networks are supported by publicly verifiable sources; (3) insider-access claims are flagged explicitly; (4) CBMT’s and UDPN’s own limitations are documented with the same rigor and notation as competitors’; (5) the paper deliberately refrains from declaring which architecture will prevail; and (6) the {S, L, I} Framework itself is a mitigation — by classifying structural properties by topology rather than by the author’s assessment, it reduces the scope for COI-influenced judgment.

detail.abstract: The tokenized-deposit interoperability landscape now encompasses twelve named networks and two competing narratives — the official-sector “singleness of money via unified ledger” thesis (BIS/IMF/FSB) and the crypto-industry vision of bridge-asset rails as the future of global settlement — neither of which evaluates architectures within a common structural framework. This paper develops the {Settlement Instrument, Ledger Topology, Intermediary Role} ({S, L, I}) Framework, which classifies any tokenized-deposit architecture by three structural elements and identifies operational properties from the configuration, separating what is determined by topology from what varies with implementation maturity. The framework yields four models — shared-ledger orchestration (I), bilateral mesh (II), native-liability bridge (III), and intermediary-token bridge (IV) — into which all eleven live networks classify unambiguously, complemented by a graph-theoretic formalization of bottleneck, robustness, and capacity-constrained flow. Each model is evaluated across five operational dimensions and synthesized through a financial-stability lens. Two findings emerge. First, Model I, the architecture with the most official-sector endorsement, scores lowest on both finality dimensions as of mid-2026, and BIS’s own literature has not acknowledged that the unified ledger is a coordination overlay, not an independent settlement architecture for retail deposits. Second, Model IV carries a structural liquidity ceiling — bounded by the bridge asset’s market depth, with non-bank sub-types additionally failing BIS’s elasticity test by regulatory construction — and unmitigated concentration risk (κ = 1). The paper formalizes the ceiling by extending Krugman’s (1980) vehicle-currency theory to digital bridge assets, validated against primary-source evidence. The paper refrains from declaring which architecture will prevail, identifying instead the developments that would change its assessment.

title: From Offline Shopping to Online Shopping in Nigeria: Evidence from African Emerging Economy
affiliations: , Unaffiliated Author, Michael Okpara University of Agriculture and Nnamdi Azikiwe University - Faculty of Management Sciences

detail.title: From Offline Shopping to Online Shopping in Nigeria: Evidence from African Emerging Economy
detail.abstract: Purpose-The study builds on studies in online shopping. Existing studies in online shopping proved that it is an attraction to shoppers. In Nigeria's emerging economy the increasing Internet penetration does not equate with intention to use online shopping because it is not really used by users for online shopping. Consumers are considering it unattractive because of serious concerns that border on product quality of online shops and poor know-how on e-tech. The study sought to explore factors that could mitigate challenges to successful online shopping in Nigeria's emerging economy. Design/methodology/approach-Online survey method was used to sample 246 respondents. Measurement items were adapted from related literature. Confirmatory factor analysis and content validity were used to check the reliability and validity. A set of fit indices were used to check the goodness of fit. Data was analysed using structural equation model. Findings-Results indicate direct effects of consumer attitude, perceived usefulness and social influence on intention to use online shopping with consumer attitude shown to have a greater degree of importance towards intention to use online shopping. Thus, consumers' attitude of browsing online and going offline for purchases is dependent on attitude of like or dislike. Perceived ease of use, social influence and perceived usefulness had an indirect positive effect on consumer attitude to intention to use online shopping. Social influence is indicated to have a direct positive effect on perceived ease of use. Also perceived ease of use had a positive and direct effect on perceived usefulness. Research limitations/implications-The sample size is not large enough and the use of snowball sampling limits representativeness. Practical implications-The study indicated vital factors African emerging economies like Nigeria can use to improve consumer confidence towards intention to use online shopping and drive cashless policies. Several studies have missed the indirect effect of referents (social influence) on adoption of technology. The study proved that it can produce indirect effect as well as direct effect on intention to use online shopping. Originality/value-Several studies have missed the indirect effect of referents (social influence) on adoption of technology. The study proved that it can produce indirect effect as well as direct effect on online shopping.

title: User Behaviour on Continuance Intention to Use M-Commerce in African Context: Mediating Effect of Perceived Value
affiliations: , Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Nnamdi Azikiwe University and Alex Ekwueme Federal University Ndufu-Alike (AE-FUNAI)

detail.title: User Behaviour on Continuance Intention to Use M-Commerce in African Context: Mediating Effect of Perceived Value
detail.abstract: Purpose-There has been a huge fluctuation in online marketplace that suggests inconsistencies of mcommerce usage. The study investigates user behaviour to continued patronage of m-commerce and the mediating role of perceived value. Design/methodology/approach-The study aimed to use adapted questionnaire and online version to pool data from respondents that has internet profile and conducts m-commerce. The hypotheses were proven through the use of structural equation model. Findings-In this paper performance expectancy and user satisfaction are major determinants of continuance intention to use m-commerce in African context while perceived value partially mediate the relationship between the variables. Research limitations/implications-Cross-sectional survey and the small sample size that was used calls for caution in generalisation. Practical implications-With the mediating influence of perceived value, attention is directed to the role of value perception of m-commerce users. Keeping and increasing continuance usage requires pleasurable offerings and value indices that influence their subjective perceptions. Social implications-The significance of the mediating variable highlights the social value dimension of users' value perception given that it can help to deepen the continuous usage of m-commerce. Originality/value-The predictive power of 78.5% continuance intention demonstrates inclusion of factors with better predictive accuracy. Importantly, the significance of perceived value as a mediator demonstrates the importance of valuing not only the direct impacts of the variables but also the indirect roles that impacts continuance intention of m-commerce in African context.

title: Backup Behaviour: Rational Distrust as a Consumer Response to Infrastructural Volatility

detail.title: Backup Behaviour: Rational Distrust as a Consumer Response to Infrastructural Volatility
detail.abstract:
This paper names a consumer behaviour it calls backup behaviour, the deliberate holding of redundant provider relationships as insurance against institutional failure. Drawing on an illustrative survey of 82 Nigerian adults, it documents a substantial gap between the financial accounts people hold and the far smaller number they actively use. Respondents held an average of 3.57 bank accounts but actively used only 1.91, a gap of 1.66 accounts per person. This gap is not multi-homing, the opportunity-driven use of several providers to capture the benefit of each. It is a risk-driven response to an environment where any single provider may fail in a moment that matters. Established brand relationship frameworks read multiple costly relationships as divided loyalty or weak commitment. In a volatile market they signal the opposite, a rational distrust of the environment and a fallback held ready.
The paper grounds the pattern in loss aversion rather than loyalty, sets it against national data showing tens of millions of dormant bank accounts, and argues that this is what rational consumer brand relationships look like where institutional reliability cannot be assumed. The financial case is where the behaviour can be measured, but the same logic runs through how Nigerians layer electricity, connectivity, and every other unreliable service.

title: A Silver Lining? Consumer Preferences over Human-made and AI-generated Production in Two Domains
affiliations: Newcastle University Business School, Newcastle University, Newcastle University and Technical University Hamburg-Harburg (TUHH)

detail.title: A Silver Lining? Consumer Preferences over Human-made and AI-generated Production in Two Domains
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence can now generate outputs that were once the preserve of human labour. Yet well-documented algorithm aversion raises the possibility of consumer bias in favour of human-made work. This paper uses incentivised experimental auctions and state-of-the-art generative AI models to compare consumer valuations for human-made versus AI-generated images and poetry, sold respectively as physical prints and on mugs. In a broad population sample from the UK, we observe a premium for human-made work in consumer valuations. However, among the youngest participants we observe no such premium, mirroring the findings of a laboratory study with student participants. Demand for AI-generated outputs varies with individuals' attitudes toward AI. Whether the age pattern reflects ageing or cohort replacement will determine whether consumer preferences can help sustain human labour.

title: Navigating the Waste-Markdown Tradeoff: A Field Experiment Comparing Price and Information Interventions
affiliations: Tilburg University, Tilburg University, Tilburg University and Tilburg University

detail.title: Navigating the Waste-Markdown Tradeoff: A Field Experiment Comparing Price and Information Interventions
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Food retailers can cut downstream waste by selling more at-risk inventory before it expires. They have two operational levers to do so: pricing (which near-expiry products are marked down, when, and how deeply) and information (how visible markdowns are to shoppers). We ask which reduces waste, and how. 
Methodology/results: We conduct a field experiment at a European supermarket chain. An iterative crowdsourcing procedure generated two interventions: centralized discounting and dynamic pricing. Centralized discounting moves near-expiry discounted products to a high-traffic refrigerated bin while preserving the retailer's static discount rule; dynamic pricing, implemented through three competing systems, varies markdown timing and depth on the regular shelf. Using store-week data on markdowns, sales, deliveries, and waste, we estimate difference-in-differences effects relative to control stores. The two interventions that successfully reduce waste act at different stages of the funnel. Centralized discounting raises the sell-through of already-discounted products by making them more visible to shoppers, cutting waste without additional margin sacrifice. Among the three dynamic-pricing systems, only the one that expands markdown coverage—bringing more at-risk products into the discount channel—reduces waste enough to lower total financial loss; the other two cut markdown costs but not waste, with no reliable improvement in total financial loss. 
Managerial implications: The results offer two lessons. First, dynamic pricing is not one intervention but a family of strategies: retailers should evaluate dynamic-pricing systems by how many near-expiry products they convert into rescued sales, rather than by algorithmic sophistication alone. Second, centralized discounting shows that improving the information environment can reduce waste while holding the discount rule fixed: by making markdowns salient, it raises sell-through and lowers waste without algorithmic pricing and added margin sacrifice, while achieving roughly two-thirds the savings of the only dynamic-pricing system that reduces waste.

title: From Structural Equation Modelling to Double Machine Learning: Robustness Analysis for Survey-Based Research
affiliations: University of Southern Queensland, , University of Southern Queensland and University of Southern Queensland

detail.title: From Structural Equation Modelling to Double Machine Learning: Robustness Analysis for Survey-Based Research

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval received for the survey data collected
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received

detail.abstract: Structural equation modelling (SEM) is widely used in survey-based business and information systems research to assess latent constructs and theory-driven structural relationships. However, SEM path significance is obtained within a particular model specification and may not show whether findings remain stable under alternative estimation frameworks. This study develops and demonstrates a staged robustness analysis framework that connects SEM, ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, and Double Machine Learning (DML). SEM is first used to refine the measurement structure and estimate the robustness-baseline SEM model, in which the full theory-specified structural path system is retained for downstream robustness analysis before final structural path evaluation. OLS regression is then applied to SEM-derived construct scores as a transparent regression benchmark. Finally, DML-style residualisation is used to examine whether each tested focal relationship remains stable after flexible machine-learning-based adjustment for observed controls. Learner-sensitivity checks compare Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machine learners, and selected reverse-direction diagnostics are used to examine directional sensitivity. The framework is demonstrated using a FinTech Digital Customer Intimacy survey model. The findings identify which relationships are stable across SEM, OLS, and DML-style checks, and which require more cautious interpretation. A reproducible Google Colab workbook and generated result files are publicly available, providing a reusable template that researchers and students can adapt to other survey-based latent-construct studies. The paper contributes a practical robustness workflow and interpretation guide for survey-based researchers seeking to complement SEM with conventional and machine-learning-based robustness checks.

title: Shadow Data in Higher Education: A Socio-technical Framework for Governing Unused and Under-managed Third-party Digital Assets
affiliations: Coastline Community College

detail.title: Shadow Data in Higher Education: A Socio-technical Framework for Governing Unused and Under-managed Third-party Digital Assets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No financial gains are associated with the research
declarations.ethicsApproval: There are no human subjects invovled
declarations.funderStatement: Research was not funded

detail.abstract: Higher education institutions operate through dense ecosystems of learning management systems, advising platforms, student success tools, remote proctoring services, customer relationship management applications, cloud productivity suites, tutoring platforms, library systems, assessment tools, vendor dashboards, and artificial intelligence services. These systems generate and retain large amounts of data that may be technically available to an institution but remain unused, inaccessible, low trust, weakly governed, or outside routine institutional stewardship. This article develops shadow data as a theoretical construct for higher education. Shadow data is defined as data generated, collected, stored, exported, integrated, or made available through institutional or third-party digital systems but not meaningfully accessed, analyzed, governed, or used because of quality, relevance, ownership, access, interoperability, privacy, ethical, contractual, or capacity constraints. The article distinguishes shadow data from dark data, shadow information technology, shadow artificial intelligence, data exhaust, and governed institutional data. It integrates sociotechnical systems theory, information governance, institutional theory, platformization, contextual integrity, learning analytics ethics, and responsible artificial intelligence governance to explain why shadow data emerges and why it matters. The article proposes a typology, conceptual model, theoretical propositions, practitioner checklist, and research agenda. It argues that shadow data is not only a technical backlog. It is a governance, privacy, equity, institutional effectiveness, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence readiness issue that requires lifecycle stewardship, vendor accountability, transparent data classification, and cross-functional institutional ownership.

title: Modeling Approaches for Production Planning of Perishable Products Under Depreciation Effects
affiliations: Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul, Universidade de São Paulo and Universidade Federal de São Carlos (UFScar)

detail.title: Modeling Approaches for Production Planning of Perishable Products Under Depreciation Effects

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso do Sul - UFMS/Brazil, by the São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP grants 2024/07482-5 and 2022/05803-3), and by the Brazilian agency National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq grants 301967/2025-3 and 304618/2023-3). The research was conducted using the computational resources of the Center for Mathematical Sciences Applied to Industry – CeMEAI (FAPESP grant 2013/07375-0).

detail.abstract: This paper addresses a production planning problem faced by Brazilian meat companies. Several perishable products are manufactured on production lines that share limited resources, including tools, machines, and workers. Resource scarcity forces managers to decide which lines to operate in each period while respecting capacity constraints. The problem also involves inventory holding costs, backlogging, sequence-dependent setup times and costs, and costs associated with assembling production lines. Product perishability further complicates decision-making, as major customers (supermarkets and restaurant chains) avoid accepting items close to their shelf life at standard prices, making discount policies based on product age necessary. To address this problem, we propose a modeling and optimization approach. First, a price-and age-dependent demand function is developed, combining regular market prices and forecasted demand. Next, a customer service policy common in the target market is formalized, leading to an age-dependent pricing function. These prices are incorporated as parameters in a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model representing operational production planning decisions. A computational study evaluates the proposed approach and provides managerial insights into how price depreciation influences production planning.

title: The U.S.-China Strategic Import Risk Index (SIRI): A Dynamic Measure of U.S. Sector-Level Strategic Import Vulnerability
affiliations: Howard University

detail.title: The U.S.-China Strategic Import Risk Index (SIRI): A Dynamic Measure of U.S. Sector-Level Strategic Import Vulnerability

keywords: Strategic Import Vulnerability Supply Chain Resilience U

detail.abstract: Growing concerns over economic security have increased the demand for high-frequency measures of strategic import vulnerability. Existing indicators typically capture only individual dimensions of supply-chain risk, including logistics disruptions, supplier concentration, and geopolitical uncertainty, but rarely integrate these complementary dimensions into a unified measure of strategic vulnerability. This paper develops the Strategic Import Risk Index (SIRI), a sector-specific, high-frequency measure of U.S. strategic import vulnerability associated with dependence on Chinese supply chains. Using monthly HS-6 bilateral trade data, the SIRI integrates structural import exposure, supplier dependence, substitution fragility, supplier instability, and macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions within a transparent framework designed for real-time monitoring. The empirical analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity across strategic sectors. Advanced Manufacturing and Electronics, Battery and Energy Storage Materials, and Medical and Health-Security Supplies are more sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and broader supply-chain disruptions, whereas Critical Minerals and Advanced Materials respond primarily to trade policy interventions and geopolitical developments. Validation exercises further show that the SIRI provides incremental explanatory power and improves recursive out-of-sample forecasts of U.S. Industrial Production relative to existing measures of supply-chain disruptions and geopolitical risk. By integrating structural dependence with evolving external conditions within a sectorspecific, high-frequency, and dynamic measure, the SIRI provides a new framework for measuring strategic import vulnerability. The proposed index offers researchers and policymakers a practical tool for monitoring emerging supply-chain risks and informing economic-security policy in an increasingly fragmented global economy.

title: Involuntary Unemployment Due to Permanent Disability Risk and Unemployment Insurance Design
affiliations: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) - Department of Industrial and Management Engineering, Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) and

detail.title: Involuntary Unemployment Due to Permanent Disability Risk and Unemployment Insurance Design
detail.abstract: We study optimal retirement, consumption, and portfolio choice for an individual who faces permanent disability risk that triggers involuntary unemployment. The disability and labor-income risks are not spanned by the traded bond and stock; a personalized unemployment insurance policy that pays the wealth gap at the disability event completes the market, but is sold at a loaded premium. Departing from a constant loading, we introduce a proportional loading and derive an analytical upper bound above which the individual prefers to remain uninsured and the insurance market is no longer viable. We obtain a semi-analytic solution by reducing the problem to a single free-boundary problem and applying a convex-duality transformation. A higher disability intensity lowers the critical wealth level and the consumption ratio, prompting earlier retirement. The premium rate is hump-shaped in disability intensity, and the payout is larger when post-disability leisure is lower.

title: WHERE THE BRAND BREAKS: How Employees Reject Brand Positioning in the Brand's Own Words

detail.title: WHERE THE BRAND BREAKS: How Employees Reject Brand Positioning in the Brand's Own Words

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The author has no employment, consulting, ownership, funding, or other relationship with Lululemon Athletica, Glassdoor, or any organization named in this paper, and no such relationship influenced the design, analysis, or conclusions. The work was carried out as part of doctoral study at the Haskayne School of Business, University of Calgary.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, recruitment, interviews, or the collection of private or identifiable information. It analyzes only publicly available, non-identifiable secondary text: employee reviews posted publicly on Glassdoor and the company's own public brand and corporate materials. No individual is named or identifiable; quotations are reproduced without usernames or personal identifiers and are tagged only by year and a broad role category. On this basis the study relied on public secondary data and did not require research ethics board review.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external, institutional, or commercial funding. It was conducted by the author as part of the Doctor of Business Administration program at the Haskayne School of Business, University of Calgary, using only publicly available data and no paid data sources.

detail.abstract: Marketing owns the customer brand and Human Resources owns the employer brand, and the two literatures rarely meet. This paper tests one against the other. I reconstruct the customer-facing brand positioning Lululemon projected from 2021 to 2025, expressed in Zyman's four elements, and read 1,994 public Glassdoor reviews from the same window, split into 4,529 passages, against it, coding each passage as affirming, contradicting, or staying silent on each element. The pattern is sharp: the one element backed by budgeted, observable programs (Support) is affirmed 85 percent of the time it is engaged, while the abstract identity claims that live only in marketing language draw more contradiction than affirmation. Where employees reject the brand, they use the brand's own positioning vocabulary as the evidence, a move I name brand legitimacy rejection. The study contributes that construct and a free, public diagnostic for testing whether a positioning is lived inside the firm.

title: The State of AI-Readiness on Business Websites (2026): A Large-Scale Measurement of AI-Crawler Permission, llms.txt Adoption, and Structured-Data Readiness
affiliations: Axion Deep Labs

detail.title: The State of AI-Readiness on Business Websites (2026): A Large-Scale Measurement of AI-Crawler Permission, llms.txt Adoption, and Structured-Data Readiness

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is affiliated with Axion Deep Labs, Inc. and its Axion Deep Digital unit, which provides SEO and AI visibility services and operates a related website audit tool. This commercial interest is disclosed for transparency. The study measures publicly observable website signals using automated, deterministic code and a preregistered analysis plan; no client data or paid placement influenced the results.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study involves no human or animal subjects. It measures only publicly accessible website resources (homepage HTML, robots.txt, and llms.txt) via polite, rate-limited HTTP and collects no personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted and funded internally by Axion Deep Labs, Inc.

detail.abstract: As AI answer engines become a discovery channel, a website's ability to participate is gated by three public, machine-checkable signals: whether it permits AI crawlers (robots.txt), whether it guides them (llms.txt), and whether it is structured for machine identification (schema.org). We define AI-readiness operationally as adoption of these three public signals, and measure them across a stratified sample of local-business websites (n = 766, 10 verticals, 15 cities) drawn from OpenStreetMap. Among reachable sites, adoption of the structured-data signals designed to make a business machine-identifiable is low: review/AggregateRating markup appears on 9% of homepages (95% CI 7-11) and FAQ markup on 4% (3-6). The modal business scores 2 of 10 on a pre-specified AI-Readiness index (42% of reachable sites): it does not block AI crawlers, but exposes no schema, reviews markup, or llms.txt. Readiness varies sharply by vertical: accounting firms show 0% review and 0% Person markup (0 of 27; Wilson 95% CI 0-12 for each), non-overlapping with legal firms (review 26%, CI 18-35; Person 31%, CI 22-41); accounting is the only vertical simultaneously at zero review, zero Person, and lowest identity markup. llms.txt adoption is 25% (22-29), of which at least 28% carries a tool-generation signature rather than being authored. Unlike publishers, local businesses rarely block AI crawlers (4%, CI 3-6). Figures replicated across 149-, 487-, and 766-site samples. The dataset, code, and codebooks are released openly.

title: Orphan Risks at the Frontier of Artificial Intelligence: What Diverging Safety and Compliance Frameworks Reveal About How AI Companies Choose the Risks they Prioritize

detail.title: Orphan Risks at the Frontier of Artificial Intelligence: What Diverging Safety and Compliance Frameworks Reveal About How AI Companies Choose the Risks they Prioritize
detail.abstract: Companies developing some of the world's most powerful artificial intelligence systems are surprisingly diligent in how they map out the risks their technologies present. Yet the risk landscape that lies between emerging frontier models and their economically successful and societally beneficial deployment is becoming increasingly hard to navigate. Complicating this further, many frontier AI companies maintain more than one account of what could go wrong with their technologies. This paper documents the divergence between these accounts by comparing safety and compliance documents published by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Meta between 2023 and 2026, and considers what the resulting record reveals about how these companies select the risks they manage. As these documents are timestamped and archived, they provide a valuable public record of institutional risk selection in progress. From this record the paper identifies four filters that determine which risks tend to survive in self-authored frameworks (measurability, severity, auditability and competitive cost) and introduces the "safety differential" as the gap between the risk landscape a company selects for itself, and the one regulators select for it. While acute, quantifiable risks appear across documents, less tractable risks such as harmful manipulation are articulated fluently where law compels disclosure, yet remain absent from most selfchosen frameworks. This is an exclusion that follows from how these institutions define risk. Drawing on scholarship on institutional risk selection and the framework of risk innovation, the paper shows how redefining risk as a threat to value can help explain how risks become "orphan risks," how it indicates where future blindsides may occur, and how it points to lightweight tools for de-orphaning risks that frontier AI's safety apparatuses are not currently organized to address.

title: From Handshakes to Hashtags: Fostering Digital Human Touch in Business-to-Business Interactions

detail.title: From Handshakes to Hashtags: Fostering Digital Human Touch in Business-to-Business Interactions
detail.abstract: In the contemporary business landscape, where business interactions are progressively migrating to virtual environments, the ability to convey human touch without physical proximity has emerged as a critical yet under-explored phenomenon. This study conceptualizes Digital Human Touch as a relational construct, exploring how empathy, authenticity, warmth, and care are enacted through digital channels. The study's research design encompasses dyadic buyersupplier interviews conducted prior to, during, and following the onset of the pandemic with a large-scale analysis of customer reviews. The findings identify core dimensions of Digital Human Touch: digital authenticity, warmth and care, and openness in communication; during the pandemic, also: forgiveness and tolerance, and reconciliation. The post-Covid-19 emergence of real-time connectedness was also identified. The findings indicate that Digital Human Touch fosters relational continuity and value co-creation. By challenging the assumption that human touch always requires physical interaction, this study contributes to the advancement of theory on relationship management.

title: The Cognitive Unit : A New Unit of Analysis for the AI Age-From Individual to Human-Agent Value Creation

detail.title: The Cognitive Unit : A New Unit of Analysis for the AI Age-From Individual to Human-Agent Value Creation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently, with no financial or personal relationships with any organization that could have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a theoretical and philosophical study involving no human participants, patient data, clinical trials, or empirical data collection. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was self-funded by the author as part of independent scholarly work conducted under the WorldValue research platform.

detail.abstract: Since the Industrial Revolution, the social sciences have implicitly treated the Individual as the basic unit of analysis for value creation, labor, organization, and civilization. The proliferation of generative artificial intelligence and multi-agent orchestration is reorganizing how cognitive labor-memory, reasoning, drafting, and execution-is performed, increasingly distributing it across human operators and networks of AI agents. This paper introduces the Cognitive Unit as a new unit of analysis for the AI age: a value-creating system composed of a sovereign human observer coordinating multiple AI agents, external memory, and cognitive workflows. Drawing on secondorder cybernetics (von Foerster, 2003), process philosophy (Whitehead, 1929/1978), and the author's prior work on Personal Sovereign AI and the Process-Paradox Framework (Lin, 2026a, 2026b), the paper argues that the Cognitive Unit, rather than the Individual, increasingly constitutes the basic unit through which value is created in contemporary economies. The paper develops the internal architecture of the Cognitive Unit, proposes three testable propositions concerning its productivity, and traces its implications for economics, sociology, management, political science, education, and civilizational theory.

title: Research and Development (R&D) Methods: ADDIE Model, Dick & Carey Model, and ASSURE Model -Definitions, Types, Advantages, Disadvantages, and Applications
affiliations: and University of Graha Nusantara

detail.title: Research and Development (R&D) Methods: ADDIE Model, Dick & Carey Model, and ASSURE Model -Definitions, Types, Advantages, Disadvantages, and Applications

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no conflicts of interest regarding the publication of this article. The authors have no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a literature-based review and comparative analysis that did not involve human participants, animals, personal data, or clinical experiments. Therefore, ethical approval and informed consent were not required in accordance with institutional and international research ethics guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding from public, commercial, or not-for-profit organizations. The study was conducted independently by the authors without financial support.

detail.abstract: Research and Development (R&D) in education is a systematic process designed to create or improve educational products, models, or training programs based on field needs. Instructional design models serve as essential frameworks guiding this development process. This article provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of three prominent instructional design models commonly applied in educational R&D: the ADDIE Model, the Dick & Carey Model, and the ASSURE Model. Each model is examined in terms of its definition, procedural structure, types, advantages, limitations, and practical applications. The analysis reveals that while all three models share core phases of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation, they differ significantly in their level of detail, flexibility, and contextual suitability. ADDIE offers a generic and flexible framework, Dick & Carey provides a highly systematic and interconnected systems approach, and ASSURE emphasizes technology integration and learner-centered classroom application. Understanding these distinctions enables researchers and practitioners to select the most appropriate model based on their specific R&D objectives, product complexity, and contextual constraints.

title: Geopolitical Stress Regimes and Financial Structure in Gulf Energy Exporters: A Quantitative and Stochastic Analysis of Qatar and Oman vis-à-vis Global Financial Conditions

detail.title: Geopolitical Stress Regimes and Financial Structure in Gulf Energy Exporters: A Quantitative and Stochastic Analysis of Qatar and Oman vis-à-vis Global Financial Conditions
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how geopolitical risk is transmitted into the financial markets of two structurally distinct Gulf energy exporters, Qatar and Oman, over a sample running from January 2007 to April 2026. The comparison is designed around a productive asymmetry, Qatar's export base is liquefied natural gas, contractually anchored and logistically irreversible through the Strait of Hormuz. At the same time, Oman's is conventional crude oil, more cyclically volatile but partially re-routable outside the Strait. The paper combines Markov-switching regime identification, GJR-GARCH volatility modelling, a nine-variable structural VAR, Chow and Bai-Perron structural break tests, a multi-asset event study and Merton jump-diffusion Monte Carlo simulation to characterise the channels through which the Caldara and Iacoviello (2022) Geopolitical Risk Index propagates into Gulf equity, sovereign bond, currency and commodity markets.


The paper develops a real options framework, building on Dixit and Pindyck (1994) and Merton (1976), to explain why QatarEnergy continues to commit US$30 billion to the North Field LNG expansion despite a structurally oversupplied global LNG market and translates the full set of empirical findings into a volatility-conditioned asset allocation framework, a contingent sovereign bond entry signal and a scenario-based Monte Carlo simulation spanning de-escalation, sustained tension and acute closure outcomes for the Hormuz episode.

title: Learning Optimal Suggested Donation Menus with (Misspecified) Linear Bandits
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management,  and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management

detail.title: Learning Optimal Suggested Donation Menus with (Misspecified) Linear Bandits
detail.abstract: Nonprofits generate billions annually through digital fundraising, with suggested donation menus playing a central role. Though these menus influence donor behavior, they can have a mixed impact on overall revenue. This creates a core challenge: how to efficiently identify the optimal menu from among the large space of combinations. We cast this challenge as a multi-armed bandit problem, with menus as arms and donations as rewards. To enable cross-learning-where the reward from one menu provides insight into the rewards of similar menus-we introduce a behavioral property which enables a reformulation to an online longest path problem in a directed acyclic graph. For cases where this property perfectly captures donor behavior, we construct a tailored version of the Optimism in the Face of Uncertainty for Linear Bandits (OFUL) algorithm (Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011) which provides strong guarantees on expected regret. For arbitrary donor behavior (where rewards can be non-linear), we propose a new algorithm: Pessimistic Optimism for Misspecified Linear Bandits (POML). Our algorithm integrates aspects of OFUL with the well-known Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) algorithm, achieving a best-of-both-worlds regret bound: in the absence of misspecification, POML is comparable to OFUL. As misspecification grows, POML's regret bound remains sublinear, becoming similar to UCB. We support our theoretical development with a numerical case study based on real donation data, which highlights the value of our algorithmic idea. Our framework provides a principled approach for nonprofits to enhance online fundraising revenue while minimizing experimental costs.

title: The Reversibility Frontier of Capital Centralisation

detail.title: The Reversibility Frontier of Capital Centralisation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, human data, or animals. Therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The solvency-rule research programme treats monetary and financial conditions as a selection mechanism: they affect not only the volume of accumulation but also which capitals survive, acquire and are absorbed. We develop its dynamic counterpart by modelling acquisitions as coagulation and effective deconsolidation as fragmentation. In the pure Marcus-Lushnikov benchmark with product kernel K β (x, y) = κ(xy) β , the common scale κ changes time while the size-selectivity exponent β changes relative hazards. Classical coagulation theory places the ordinary pure-gelation boundary at β = 1/2. Pure coagulation, however, cannot explain irreversibility because it removes every reverse transition from the state space. We add binary fragmentation at rate φx γ and write ρ = φ/κ. At fixed total mass, the generator factors as κ(C β + ρF γ): the invariant distribution depends on (β, ρ, γ), whereas κ fixes the physical clock. The finite chain is irreducible and has a unique invariant distribution, so permanent hysteresis is impossible after baseline parameters are restored. The relevant objects are instead stationary centralisation, finite-horizon memory and large-system metastability. We derive a hierarchy of local post-break-up races. For an asymptotically homogeneous acquisition kernel of degree λ and a regularly varying fragmentation rate of index γ, direct remerger relative to renewed fragmentation scales as N λ-γ-1 , up to slowly varying factors. For the product kernel, the boundary is γ = 2β-1. We then include the first attachment of either fragment to the surrounding economy. If the background β-moment scales as N s , the strongest coagulative first-event channel relative to renewed fragmentation is governed by max{2β-1, β + s-1}γ. In a diffuse background (s = 1), attachment changes asymptotic orientation at γ = β. This second line identifies a local interruption of further fragmentation, not by itself restoration of the original block or long-run persistence. Corrected continuous-time simulations are validated against an exact stationary distribution for N = 5, use both dispersed and concentrated initial conditions, and report Monte Carlo uncertainty. They illustrate an increasing operational frontier and show that lower fragmentation scalability lengthens, but need not make permanent, post-shock memory. The theory thus separates formation, direct repair, first-event accretion, eventual reversibility and operator-level autonomy.

title: Public Financial Competence in Democratic Societies: Concept, Measurement, and Evidence
affiliations: University of Turin

detail.title: Public Financial Competence in Democratic Societies: Concept, Measurement, and Evidence
detail.abstract: Citizens participate in economic life not only as consumers and market participants but also as contributors to and beneficiaries of collective arrangements. Through taxation, public expenditure, and democratic representation, they are involved in decisions concerning the production, financing, and allocation of public resources. Building on insights from the literatures on civic education, economic citizenship, and financial education, the paper develops a conceptual framework and a corresponding indicator of economic competence in the public finance domain. Public Financial Competence is defined as the knowledge and reasoning ability that enables citizens to understand, evaluate, and participate in the processes through which public resources are raised, allocated, and governed in democratic societies. Using evidence from a survey conducted in Italy, the paper examines the distribution of public financial competence in the population, and its relationship with civic responsibility, tax morale, interest in politics, and democratic values. More broadly, the paper argues that knowledge of public finance and understanding of fiscal mechanisms may represent an important component of economic citizenship in contemporary democracies.

detail.abstract:
The introduction of Net Promoter Score (NPS) into political campaigns, herein coined pNPS, offers a transformative prospect for enhancing voter engagement, fostering democratic accountability, and providing insights for data-driven decision-making. Employing ideas from sociology, political science, and marketing paradigms, this study explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementations of pNPS. This research provides a thorough analysis of using pNPS to label voters as Promoters, Passives, or Detractors, allowing political campaigns to adjust their strategies and resource allocation accordingly.
The study delves into survey design, data collection, and analytic techniques, as well as methodological issues related to pNPS implementation. It also explores how pNPS affects democratic processes, including its potential to improve political accountability, facilitate informed decision-making, and rekindle citizen-rep relationships. Finally, by providing a fresh viewpoint on engaging pNPS for promoting a more involved, responsive, and inclusive democratic environment, this research adds to the continuing conversation on the nexus between data-driven strategies and political campaigns. It emphasizes the importance of going beyond the basic NPS formula to consider the potential of Passives, employing rigorous quantitative assessment methods, and adopting a context-dependent approach to benchmarks.

title: Bankruptcy Law Penalties and Board Independence

detail.title: Bankruptcy Law Penalties and Board Independence

publicationDetails.journalName: Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: A large theoretical literature suggests that bankruptcy law penalties can reduce agency problems, yet evidence remains scarce. To provide evidence, I examine whether firms implement independent directors as a substitute when penalties are eliminated. For identification, I exploit that penalties are relevant only for risky firms. Across countries, board independence is negatively related to penalties, but only among risky firms. Comparing board independence of risky and safe firms around bankruptcy reforms in Germany, Italy, and the US confirms the results. Economically, risky firms increase the number of independent directors by 21% relative to safe firms following the elimination of penalties.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decisions that affect individuals, organisations, and critical public services. As regulatory expectations for trustworthy AI continue to expand, transparency has become a central requirement for demonstrating fairness, accountability, explainability, and regulatory compliance. However, organisations face a fundamental governance dilemma. While legal and regulatory frameworks require meaningful transparency regarding automated decision-making, excessive disclosure may expose proprietary algorithms, commercially sensitive information, cybersecurity controls, and intellectual property, thereby increasing the risk of model extraction, reverse engineering, adversarial attacks, and competitive disadvantage. Existing governance frameworks recognise both transparency and confidentiality as important principles but offer limited practical guidance on how much information to disclose and to whom. This paper introduces the Safe Transparency Disclosure Framework (STDF), a governance framework designed to operationalise transparency while protecting organisational assets and maintaining public trust. Rather than treating transparency as a binary choice between disclosure and secrecy, the framework adopts a risk-based approach that classifies information into mandatory, conditional, restricted, and prohibited categories for disclosure. detail.abstract: Introduction: High turnover among skilled professionals in the Nigerian health and development NGO sector poses a substantial threat to public health interventions. This emigration, locally termed "japa," is primarily attributed to economic factors. This study investigated an alternative organizational driver. We assessed whether management transparency predicts organizational commitment and if this relationship varies between Indigenous and International NGOs. Methods: We conducted a quantitative cross-sectional survey of 397 mid-to-senior NGO professionals across Nigeria. The sample included 252 staff from INGOs and 145 from Indigenous NGOs. We used an adapted Rawlins (2009) Transparency Scale and the Allen & Meyer (1990) Three-Component Model. Data were analyzed using Simple Linear Regression, Independent Samples T-Tests, and Moderated Multiple Regression in SPSS. Results: Management transparency significantly predicted organizational commitment. It accounted for 50.6% of the variance (R² = .506, F = 404.333, p < .001, B = .518). Professionals in International NGOs reported higher perceived transparency than those in Indigenous NGOs (M = 3.95 vs. M = 3.48; t =-5.372, p < .001; mean difference =-0.465). Organizational type did not moderate this relationship (B = .078, p = .204). Meaning that NGO professionals want transparent leadership regardless of the organizational type. Conclusion: Management transparency functions as a measurable and universal driver of staff retention. The findings demonstrate that governance failures contribute substantially to the current workforce crisis beyond broader economic pressures. Therefore, NGO leadership must actively institutionalize downward transparency and dismantle personalized governance structures to secure long-term workforce stability.

title: The Restless Boundary of Internalization

detail.title: The Restless Boundary of Internalization
detail.abstract: The many theories of organizational boundaries, of the firm, the multinational, ownership, and the nonprofit, are usually read as rivals. This paper argues that they are one, and it makes three claims. The first is unification. Each theory holds that a boundary is decided by a disposition met by a contingency, and they differ only in the object they take to be enclosed. The unification is not vacuous, because it excludes accounts that make a boundary a matter of chance, of situation alone, or of fixed nature alone. Seeing the structure lets a result established for one boundary be read across to the others with only the object changed. The second claim is symmetry, and it does not follow from the first. The object a form encloses has two sides, a gain that may be taken and a loss that may be borne, and a form is bound to one of them. A firm bound to the gain and a nonprofit forbidden to distribute a surplus are mirror images of one structure, moving for opposite reasons. The third claim is motion. Because a disposition is a standing allegiance to one side of a two-sided object, the internalizer cannot be satisfied once and for all, and its own movement generates the next occasion it must answer, so the boundary does not rest. It moves wherever the rules of the moment allow, and is held in place by its contingencies while the disposition presses on it still.

detail.title: Bankruptcy Law and Firm Size

publicationDetails.journalName: Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Weaker creditor rights can increase credit costs and thus prompt firms to reduce debt and investment. Yet, they can reduce distress costs and thus allow firms to increase leverage and eliminate risk-reducing but unprofitable investments. We hypothesize that firm size influences the effect of creditor rights on credit costs and distress costs and thus which effect dominates. Weaker creditor rights should have a negative effect for small firms but a positive effect for large firms. Using a German bankruptcy reform, we find support for our hypothesis. Our findings reconcile mixed evidence and have important implications for optimal bankruptcy design.
