detail.abstract: Computational capacity (“compute”) has emerged as a strategically important and increasingly scarce economic input, yet markets for allocating future computational resources remain institutionally underdeveloped. This paper argues that the financialization of compute is economically inevitable, though the dominant institutional form of computational risk transfer—bespoke forward contracts, over-the-counter swaps, or exchange-traded futures—depends critically upon the degree of standardization achieved in computational markets. Drawing upon commodity derivatives, electricity markets, telecommunications capacity trading, and market microstructure, the paper develops a framework for understanding compute as a productive input possessing characteristics of both commodities and infrastructure services. The analysis evaluates candidate underlyings, pricing mechanisms, benchmark governance, and informational functions, concluding that benchmark-adjusted, cash-settled compute futures represent the most plausible mature-market equilibrium while customized forwards are likely to dominate where computational heterogeneity persists.

title: Leadership-Enabled Compliance: A Dual Pathway Through Organizational Inertia in Regulated MedTech Digital Transformation

detail.title: Leadership-Enabled Compliance: A Dual Pathway Through Organizational Inertia in Regulated MedTech Digital Transformation
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how organizational inertia shapes digital transformation outcomes in regulated medical technology (MedTech) manufacturers. It investigates the forms of inertia that impede technology adoption and examines how leadership sponsorship and the early integration of regulatory compliance work together, rather than independently, to enable transformation. Design/methodology/approach: A qualitative multiple-case study design was used, drawing on nine semi-structured interviews across three capital medical device manufacturers of different sizes (large, mid-size, and small). Participants included executives, mid-level managers, and individual contributors. Data were analyzed through a hybrid deductive-inductive coding process, moving from first-cycle process and in-vivo codes to six second-cycle empirical themes, cross-referenced against four conceptual forms of inertia. Findings: Four forms of organizational inertia emerged as interacting, mutually reinforcing mechanisms: cultural, structural, technological, and cognitive. Cultural and behavioral inertia was the most frequently coded barrier. Cognitive inertia operated as a distinct mechanism, visible through status quo assumptions and misaligned expectations about digital tools. Leadership sponsorship was the primary enabling condition, and it functioned as the mechanism that made early compliance integration possible: sponsored initiatives treated regulatory requirements as a design input from the outset, whereas unsponsored initiatives allowed compliance concerns to surface late and reinforce inertia. Leadership and compliance integration therefore operated as a dual, interdependent enabling pathway rather than as two separate enablers. Research limitations/implications: The qualitative, multi-case design (nine participants, three organizations) limits statistical generalizability. Findings reflect a single regional MedTech ecosystem and a cross-sectional design. Future research should test the inertia typology and the leadership-compliance interaction across other regulated industries, regions, and over longer implementation timelines. Practical implications: Quality and transformation leaders in regulated industries can use the four-form inertia typology to diagnose resistance sources before rollout. Securing visible executive sponsorship and using that sponsorship to integrate regulatory and compliance functions into transformation planning from the outset, rather than treating them as late-stage checkpoints, can accelerate rather than delay adoption. Social implications: Faster, well-governed digital transformation in MedTech manufacturing can improve traceability, product quality, and ultimately patient safety outcomes across the industry. Originality/value: This study offers an empirically grounded four-form inertia typology for regulated industries and clarifies the relationship between two enabling conditions that prior literature has largely treated separately: leadership sponsorship and regulatory integration. The finding that leadership sponsorship is what allows compliance to function as a design input, rather than a downstream hurdle, offers a new, interdependent lens for both scholars and practitioners of quality and change management.

title: Identification of CES Aggregators under Degenerate Relative-Input Variation

detail.title: Identification of CES Aggregators under Degenerate Relative-Input Variation

declarations.funderStatement: There are no funding interests to disclose.

detail.abstract: CES aggregators with free share weights are a workhorse of production and frontier econometrics, and applied work routinely fits them to data in which one input dominatesmulti-fuel electricity generation with token secondary fuels, trade aggregates with a dominant partner, labor aggregates with one dominant type. This paper characterizes exactly when such data identify the CES curvature and shares. The organizing fact is a scaleinvariance lemma: the identification Jacobian of the CES conditional mean depends on the data only through relative-input ratios; absolute scale variation is void. It follows that (i) under proportional input support the model is exactly observationally equivalent to a singleinput Cobb-Douglas for every value of the curvature and shares-the profile likelihood over the curvature is exactly flat, and any likelihood-ratio confidence region is the entire parameter space; (ii) at least J + 1 distinct ratio points are necessary for local identification of a J-input CES with intercept, and a determinant condition on any J + 1 ratio points is sufficient, failing only on a measure-zero analytic variety-a result we prove holds at every interior parameter point, not merely generically; (iii) under near-degenerate support (secondary inputs at a common small value ε) the deviation from the Cobb-Douglas envelope is bounded by an explicit function of order ε ρ , quantifying weak identification, and the likelihood's global maximum is attracted to the single-input boundary stratum of the share simplex, where the degeneracy is exact; and (iv) the parameters applied work typically cares about-error-component parameters, trends, and efficiency functionals in stochastic frontier applications-are constant on the identified set and hence point-identified with standard inference available after profiling. A pre-estimation diagnostic with a quantitative certificate (a smallest-singular-value bound that is robust to the pilot parameter value at which it is computed) makes the theory operational. The results rationalize, as theorems, pathologies that practitioners fitting dominant-input CES systems routinely encounter and typically report as computational findings: exactly flat curvature profiles, mode paths that depend on zero-handling conventions, and global modes attracted to single-input corners of the share simplex.

title: Welfare Interaction of Position Limits and Transaction Costs in Portfolio Choice
affiliations: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH),  and Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)

detail.title: Welfare Interaction of Position Limits and Transaction Costs in Portfolio Choice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF-2022S1A3A2A02089950).

detail.abstract: Long-horizon investors face transaction costs and position limits simultaneously, yet their welfare interaction under a fixed cost component remains largely unexplored. This paper studies their joint effect in a discrete-time portfolio problem with wealth-scaled fixed plus proportional transaction costs and a proportional cap on the risky share. Exploiting homogeneity, we reduce the problem to a one-dimensional dynamic program in the risky-asset share and solve the model across four cost cases (no costs, fixed only, proportional only, and fixed plus proportional) and several position-limit levels. The interaction is isolated by an excess joint certainty-equivalent (CE) wealth loss: the loss under both frictions minus the sum of the single-friction losses, each measured against the frictionless (Merton) benchmark. Three findings emerge. First, the position limit shifts not only the no-transaction region but also the post-trade rebalancing target, a distinct policy object that appears once fixed costs separate trading boundaries from target portfolios. Second, the welfare interaction is state-dependent: under baseline costs, the excess joint loss is positive and grows as the limit tightens (amplification); under high costs and tight limits, the loss becomes non-monotone and can change sign (offset). Third, the fixed-cost and proportional-cost cases produce qualitatively different loss profiles across the risky share, traceable to whether the rebalancing target is distinct from the trading boundary. The findings imply that joint optimization of trading costs and position limits cannot be replaced by separate optimization, and that calibrating to one cost form risks systematic bias for the other.

title: Within-firm pay dispersion, workforce productivity and retention: Evidence from the Treu Reform
affiliations: Alma Mater Studiorum University of Bologna,  and IE Business School - IE University

detail.title: Within-firm pay dispersion, workforce productivity and retention: Evidence from the Treu Reform
detail.abstract: We examine how the 1997 Treu labor reform in Italy, an externally timed institutional change, expanded firms’ scope to differentiate employment and compensation arrangements. Using more than two million matched employer-employee-year observations, we document that within-firm pay dispersion increased after the reform, with compensation rising at the top of the within-firm pay distribution and declining at the bottom. Greater post-reform pay dispersion is associated with higher workforce productivity and stronger operating performance, as well as greater workforce stability, reflected in lower employment volatility and employee turnover, higher retention, and lower separation rates. We further find that left-leaning and pro-labor sentiment attenuates both the post-reform increase in pay dispersion and the positive associations of pay dispersion with productivity, retention, and operating performance. Finally, although the reform reduced the overall share of permanent contracts, greater post-reform pay dispersion is associated with a higher share of permanent contracts, particularly among lower-paid workers. Taken together, the findings suggest that within-firm pay dispersion is not merely a wage-allocation outcome but part of a broader workforce-management and organizational-control configuration. Its organizational consequences depend on the employment practices with which pay differentiation is combined and on the institutional environment in which firms operate.

title: Light at the End of the Tunnel: Visitors' Virtual Reality versus In-Person Attraction Site Tour-Related Behavioral Intentions During and Post-COVID-19

detail.title: Light at the End of the Tunnel: Visitors' Virtual Reality versus In-Person Attraction Site Tour-Related Behavioral Intentions During and Post-COVID-19
detail.abstract: Consumer behavior is changing as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, thus compelling attraction sites to find new ways of offering safe tours to visitors. Based on protection motivation theory, we develop and test a model that examines key drivers of visitors’ COVID-19-induced social distancing behavior and its effect on their intent to use virtual reality-based (vs. in-person) attraction site tours during and post-COVID-19. Our analyses demonstrate that visitor-perceived threat severity, response efficacy, and self-efficacy raise social distancing behavior. In turn, social distancing increases (decreases) visitors’ intent to use virtual reality (in-person) tours during the pandemic. We find social distancing to boost visitors’ demand for advanced virtual tours and to raise their advocacy intentions. Our results also reveal that social distancing has no effect on potential visitors’ intent to use virtual reality vs. in-person tours post-the pandemic. We conclude by discussing vital implications that stem from our analyses.

title: Green Growth, Trade Openness, and Financial Integrity: International Evidence
affiliations: Ton Duc Thang University and Ho Chi Minh University of Banking

detail.title: Green Growth, Trade Openness, and Financial Integrity: International Evidence

keywords: and Financial Integrity: International Evidence Green growth

detail.abstract: With the quest for sustainable development alongside intensified actions against financial crime activities, the issue of maintaining the integrity of the financial sector is becoming an increasingly important concern. While green growth has been demonstrated to offer considerable environmental and economic gains, the link between green growth and money laundering risk has not been well-explored. In this study, the effect of green growth on money laundering risk and the moderating effect of trade openness are explored using panel data from 153 countries during 2012-2022. The findings show that green growth lowers the threat of money laundering greatly, indicating that the sustainable development policies do not only promote environmental protection but also increase the integrity of the financial system. On the other hand, the results indicate that an open degree of trade dampens this impact, implying that economic integration could be used to channel the flow of illicit money in the lack of monitoring and management systems. The findings are consistent with different measures and sample changes, as well as tests for endogeneity. The research adds value to current knowledge because it provides empirical evidence about the impact of green growth on financial integrity at the global level; however, the impact varies based on the degree of trade openness.

title: Prioritizing Urgent Route Requests in an Agent-Based Transportation Dispatch System

detail.title: Prioritizing Urgent Route Requests in an Agent-Based Transportation Dispatch System
detail.abstract: This research addresses the critical challenge of prioritizing urgent route requests within agentbased transportation dispatch systems operating under dynamic and time-sensitive conditions. As transportation networks face increasing pressure from real-time demand, unexpected disruptions, and the need for rapid emergency response, conventional dispatch algorithms often prove inadequate for handling high-priority requests without compromising overall system efficiency. This study proposes a multi-agent framework where autonomous intelligent agents represent vehicles, infrastructure nodes, and request entities, enabling decentralized, real-time decision-making for request prioritization. The framework incorporates a priority-based dispatching mechanism that dynamically evaluates request urgency based on temporal constraints, service criticality, and passenger needs, including those with mobility impairments. Through agent negotiation and coordination protocols, urgent requests are expedited while maintaining system-wide performance metrics such as average waiting time, throughput, and resource utilization. The proposed approach integrates auction-based priority assignment with optimization-driven trajectory planning to achieve real-time performance in high-density traffic scenarios. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the priority-aware agent-based system significantly reduces response times for urgent requests while sustaining overall service quality, outperforming conventional first-come-first-served and distance-based dispatching heuristics. This research contributes a practical framework for enhancing dispatch system resilience and responsiveness in emergency logistics, on-demand transit, and urban mobility services where time-critical request handling is paramount.

title: A Data Mining Framework for Enhanced Recommendations in Transportation Management Systems

detail.title: A Data Mining Framework for Enhanced Recommendations in Transportation Management Systems
detail.abstract: Transportation management systems increasingly rely on intelligent recommendation mechanisms to assist operators and users in making informed routing, scheduling, and modal choices. However, existing recommendation approaches often suffer from limited adaptability to dynamic traffic conditions, incomplete historical data, and an inability to capture complex hidden patterns in travel behavior. This study proposes a data mining framework designed to enhance the quality and relevance of recommendations within transportation management systems. The framework integrates multiple data mining techniques, including clustering for traveler segmentation, association rule mining for identifying frequently co-occurring route and mode choices, and classification algorithms for predicting user preferences under varying conditions. A modular architecture allows the framework to ingest heterogeneous data sources such as GPS traces, ticketing records, traffic sensor data, and weather information. The recommendation engine operates through a two-stage process: offline pattern discovery, where historical data is mined to extract behavioral and operational regularities, and online recommendation generation, where real-time inputs are matched against discovered patterns to produce context-aware suggestions. The framework is evaluated using a real-world dataset from a metropolitan public transport network spanning twelve months of operations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a 23% improvement in recommendation precision compared to baseline collaborative filtering approaches, while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for near-real-time deployment. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robustness to data sparsity, a common challenge in transportation domains where new routes or infrequent travelers present limited historical records. This research contributes a flexible, scalable, and interpretable data mining architecture that can be integrated into existing transportation management platforms to support more adaptive and user-centric decision-making.
